title: Four branches of closed work were never merged into master; they conflict pairwise
description:
Discovered while starting sized-grid-all (2026-08-10). master == origin/master == 3b6d71f, and 'git branch --no-merged master' lists four branches, every one of which carries work whose beads issue is already CLOSED:

  worktree-ordinal-int          7817043 Make Ordinal a newtype over Int
                                b897c89 Close sized-grid-upo, j23, swi, pir
  worktree-allcoord             3adbe84 Make coordPosition an Int pass (contains ordinal-int)
  worktree-seal-grid-abstraction 0ee8332 Seal the Grid abstraction (sized-grid-7uj)
  worktree-examples-build-s25   32ba97c Bring the three examples back to life (s25)
                                4767533 Fix the grid-slicing hang; gridWindows is gridTiles (61o)

So the tracker says upo/j23/swi/pir/uvd/7uj/s25/61o are done, but none of that code is on master. Anyone reading master sees the old Ordinal GADT, the exported Grid constructor, and the broken examples.

They also conflict with each other, not just with master:
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs   -- gutted by seal-grid (-350 lines, moved to a new
    src/SizedGrid/Internal/Grid.hs), extended by examples-build (+64), touched by allcoord (+32)
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs -- allcoord (26 lines), seal-grid (6)
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs       -- allcoord (98), seal-grid (34)
  - tests/Main.hs, ChangeLog.md, sized-grid.cabal -- all four

Every remaining open issue touches at least one of those files, so each new branch started from master makes the eventual integration worse. This should be resolved before any further parallel work.
acceptance_criteria: master contains the work of all four branches (or an explicit decision recorded for any branch that is to be dropped), the merged tree builds with zero warnings, and the full test suite passes.
notes:
Integration branch 'worktree-integration' is pushed and verified (2026-08-11).

All three merges done in this order: worktree-allcoord (clean), worktree-seal-grid-abstraction (conflicts in Grid/Grid.hs and Ordinal.hs), worktree-examples-build-s25 (conflict in Grid/Grid.hs). worktree-ordinal-int needed no separate merge -- worktree-allcoord already contains it.

Three defects existed only in the combination and would have been merged silently:
  1. seal-grid moved Grid/Grid.hs into a new Internal/Grid.hs, so allcoord's and examples-build's edits to Grid.hs landed in a file the other branch had emptied. Hand-ported: tabulate's V.fromListN, ifoldr/ifoldl', KnownNat x on ShrinkableGrid, the splitVectorBySize zero guard, zipLowerDim, gridWindows -> gridTiles.
  2. seal-grid added an export list to Coord.hs while allcoord added three new top-level functions to it. Textually clean, semantically broken: tabulate failed to compile and three functions were dead. coordSpaceSize and coordFromPosition are now exported, coordDigits stays internal.
  3. seal-grid turned on -Wmissing-export-lists; examples-build's new tests/Test/Tiling.hs had no export list.

Verified from a clean dist-newstyle: lib + sudoko + gameOfLife + ising-example + tests + benchmarks + README suite all build; 129 tests and the README suite pass; sudoko runs and prints 9 rows and 9 columns. Warning count is exactly master's 14, no new ones (master was never warning-free in the test suite: 5 orphans, 4 unused-matches, 2 unused-imports, 2 redundant-constraints in tests/Main.hs, 1 redundant-constraints in README.lhs).

Remaining step is not mine to take: master must move. It is a fast-forward --
    git checkout master && git merge --ff-only worktree-integration && git push
After that the four merged branches can be deleted locally and on origin.
close_reason: master fast-forwarded to the integration branch (73704d5) by Kevin on 2026-08-11. master now contains all four branches' work; tracker and master agree again.

title: ../aoc 2018/06 manhattan silently returns 0 after the HardWrap (.-.) fix
description:
BREAKING CONSUMER CHANGE, confirmed empirically against the fixed library.

sized-grid-0kf removed the 'max 0' clamp from HardWrap's (.-.) so it returns a true
signed displacement. ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs:22-26 was relying on that clamp to compute
an absolute value:

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum [dx1, dx2, dy1, dy2]
      where
        (dx1, dy1) = c1 .-. c2
        (dx2, dy2) = c2 .-. c1

OLD: dx1 = max 0 (x1-x2), dx2 = max 0 (x2-x1), so dx1 + dx2 = |x1-x2|. Correct.
NEW: dx1 = x1-x2, dx2 = x2-x1, so dx1 + dx2 = 0. Always.

Probe output against the fixed library (HardWrap 400 x HardWrap 400):
    (1,1) -> (8,3) = 0
    (8,3) -> (1,1) = 0
    (5,5) -> (5,5) = 0
    (3,4) -> (8,9) = 0

Every distance is 0, so 2018/06 produces a wrong answer rather than failing loudly.

FIX (in ../aoc, one line):

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum $ map abs [dx, dy]
      where (dx, dy) = c1 .-. c2

This is a defect in the consumer, not a reason to revert sized-grid-0kf: the old
behaviour violated the AffineSpace round-trip law and the clamp-as-abs trick only
worked by accident. But ../aoc must be patched in the same change set, or its 2018/06
answer regresses silently.

Also re-check the moorePoints call sites, which the 0kf fix was expected to IMPROVE:
  - ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 'filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1'
  - ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:51 and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:67 (both commented out)
The nubOrd workarounds may now be removable; verify before deleting them.
close_reason: Fixed ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs manhattan to take abs of a single signed diff; verified against the day's own (17,90) doctest via a scratch replica run in cabal repl, since ../aoc cannot build here (hmatrix/blas). moorePoints follow-up recorded on sized-grid-7gs: nubOrd workarounds must stay.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED in ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs. manhattan is now:

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum $ map abs [dx, dy]
      where (dx, dy) = c1 .-. c2

Verification: ../aoc cannot be built in this environment (pre-existing, unrelated:
hmatrix-0.20.2 fails to configure, 'Missing (or bad) C libraries: blas, lapack', and
every aoc executable depends on it). So the day was replicated verbatim against the
fixed library in a scratch module and run through 'cabal repl sized-grid':

    expected      : (17,90)   <- the doctest at ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs:42-43
    new manhattan : (17,90)   PASS
    old manhattan : *** Exception: Data.Foldable.maximum (for Data.IntMap): empty map

Correction to this issue's description: 2018/06 did not silently return a wrong
answer, it CRASHED. With every distance 0 the first target wins on 0 < maxBound and
every later one compares EQ, so closestIndex marks a tie and ownerGrid is all Nothing;
'areas' is then the empty IntMap and 'maximum areas' throws. The distances were indeed
all 0 (probe: (1,1)->(8,3) = 0 old, 9 new), the description was only wrong about the
failure being silent.

title: WIP gridWindows: rows work, but 'mapLowerDim gridWindows' for columns/squares takes a cartesian product
description:
Applies to the uncommitted change in src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:258-266 and its use in
sudoko/src/Main.hs:50-59.

CONFIRMED with a 4x4 stand-in for the 9x9 board:

    rows    = gridWindows board                 -- 4 results, correct
    columns = mapLowerDim gridWindows board     -- 256 results, expected 4

The first six 'columns' produced were
    [1,5,9,13] [1,5,9,14] [1,5,9,15] [1,5,9,16] [1,5,10,13] [1,5,10,14]
i.e. every combination of one cell per row, not the four actual columns.

Cause: mapLowerDim (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:221-233) ends in

    traverse (fmap unGrid . f . Grid) (splitVectorBySize ... v)

With f = [] the list applicative is the cartesian product, so n sub-grids each
yielding n windows gives n^n results. For the real 9x9 sudoko board that is
9^9 = 387,420,489 grids -- sudoko/src/Main.hs:54 'columns' and :56 'squares' will
both hang.

Fix: the intent is a zip, not a product. Use ZipList:

    columns = getZipList $ mapLowerDim (ZipList . gridWindows) board

That yields exactly 4 (resp. 9). Worth checking 'squares' the same way -- it is
'gridWindows' then 'mapLowerDim gridWindows', so it has the same defect.

Separately, gridWindows' signature is weak:
  - 'small' and 'big' are only related by 'CoordNat big `Mod` CoordNat small ~ 0';
    nothing ties the element counts to 'rest', so a caller can ask for a shape that
    does not tile the source.
  - splitVectorBySize's final clause returns a short trailing chunk rather than
    failing, so a non-dividing size silently yields a malformed last Grid.
  - The name says 'windows' but the behaviour is non-overlapping tiles. Sliding
    windows and disjoint tiles are different operations; pick one and name it.

Suggest landing this as two functions -- 'gridTiles' (disjoint, what the code does)
and a real 'gridWindows' (overlapping, stride 1) -- with the ZipList variant for
the lower-dimension case.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit 4767533 on worktree-examples-build-s25.

Root cause was as diagnosed: mapLowerDim combines per-sub-grid results with traverse, so f ~ [] is the list applicative and yields a cartesian product (4^4 = 256 at the 4x4 stand-in, 9^9 = 387,420,489 on the real board).

Landed:
  - zipLowerDim :: AllSizedKnown as => (Grid as x -> [Grid bs y]) -> Grid (c ': as) x -> [Grid (c ': bs) y], which is mapLowerDim in ZipList. 'zipLowerDim gridTiles' gives the 9 columns.
  - gridWindows renamed to gridTiles. It always cut disjoint tiles; the old name promised sliding windows. Safe rename -- sudoko was the only caller in this repo or ../aoc, and 0.3.0.0 is unpublished.
  - mapLowerDim's haddock now names the safe applicatives (Identity, Maybe) and the trap ([]), because the wrong choice is the obvious one.
  - splitVectorBySize rejects a chunk size of 0 instead of looping forever on empty prefixes.
  - tests/Test/Tiling.hs: 10 new tests covering gridTiles and zipLowerDim at 4x4 and 9x9, including a length assertion that would not have terminated before, plus one that pins mapLowerDim's cartesian-product behaviour so the two do not get folded back together. Suite is 90 tests, up from 80.
  - sudoko now prints all nine rows, columns and squares.

Two of the issue's sub-points resolved differently than suggested:
  - 'splitVectorBySize returns a short trailing chunk rather than failing' is unreachable from gridTiles: the Mod ~ 0 constraint plus the Grid length invariant means the chunk size always divides the source exactly. Documented rather than made total, since other callers in the module are equally protected.
  - The real (overlapping, stride 1) gridWindows was NOT added -- it is a new operation, not needed to fix the hang. Filed as sized-grid-3t6 (P3); shrinkGrid is already the primitive it would be built from.

Found while fixing: gameIsInvalid in the example ran allUnique over the Maybes, so two blank cells read as a duplicate and every partially-filled board was called invalid. Fixed to check the filled cells only.

title: FromJSON (Grid cs a) does not validate length, silently builds a Grid whose vector is the wrong size
description:
CONFIRMED empirically.

src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:145-151

    instance (All IsCoordLifted cs, FromJSON a) => FromJSON (Grid cs a) where
      parseJSON v = case (shape :: Shape cs) of
        ShapeNil -> Grid . V.singleton <$> parseJSON v
        ShapeCons _ -> do
          a :: [Grid (Tail cs) a] <- parseJSON v
          return $ Grid $ foldMap unGrid a

Nothing checks that the outer list has exactly CoordNat (Head cs) elements.

Probe result:
    decode "[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]" :: Maybe (Grid '[Ordinal 3, Ordinal 3] Int)
    => Just, with unGrid length 6 (type promises 9)

The whole point of the library is that the type pins the size. A decoded Grid that
breaks the invariant makes every downstream operation unsound:
  - index/gridIndex do 'v V.! coordPosition c' -> out-of-bounds exception at runtime
  - Applicative (<*>) is V.zipWith -> silently truncates
  - collapseGrid produces a ragged result

Contrast with gridFromList (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:121-132), which DOES check
'length cg == natVal (Proxy @(CoordNat (Head cs)))' and returns Nothing. FromJSON
should reuse exactly that logic.

Note the constraints are also asymmetric: ToJSON needs AllGridSizeKnown + SListI,
FromJSON needs All IsCoordLifted. FromJSON needs the KnownNat evidence to validate,
so aligning them on AllGridSizeKnown is part of the fix.

Why the test suite misses it: aesonLaws only round-trips well-formed values.
Add a negative test decoding a short/long array and asserting Nothing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. FromJSON now validates the length at every dimension and 'fail's otherwise, so a decoded Grid always satisfies the size invariant. Constraints aligned with ToJSON (AllGridSizeKnown cs, SListI cs), which is what supplies the KnownNat evidence needed to check.

Ragged input is rejected by the recursion: the outer list length is checked at each level. All three negative tests (too few rows / too many rows / ragged rows) now pass.

title: HardWrap violates AffineSpace laws: (.-.) clamps negative differences to 0
description:
CONFIRMED empirically (GHC 9.8.4, tests/probe).

src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:56-60

    HardWrap a .-. HardWrap b = max 0 $ min maxCoordSize (ordinalToNum a - ordinalToNum b)

With a=1, b=3 in HardWrap 10: (a .-. b) == 0, so b .+^ (a .-. b) == 3, not 1.
The AffineSpace law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) == a' is broken. Periodic satisfies it (control check passed).

Root cause: Diff (HardWrap n) = Integer should be a *signed displacement*, but (.-.) clamps
it into the coordinate range. Clamping belongs in (.+^) only, never in (.-.).

Downstream impact (real, observed in ../aoc):
  - moorePoints 1 at a HardWrap corner returns 9 points, only 4 distinct.
  - ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 has to write 'filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1'.
  - ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs abandon moorePoints entirely and
    hand-roll neighborsOf with 'toEnum nr :| toEnum nc :| EmptyCoord'.

Why the test suite misses it: tests/Test/Utils.hs:98-110 affineSpaceLaws only checks
'a .+^ zeroV == a' and 'a .-. a == zeroV'. Both hold under clamping.

Fix sketch:
  - (.-.) returns the true signed difference (no clamp).
  - (.+^) keeps clamping, OR HardWrap stops being an AffineSpace and grows a partial
    offset API returning Maybe (see the 'safe neighbour offset' issue).
  - Strengthen affineSpaceLaws with the round-trip law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a'.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. HardWrap's (.-.) now returns the true signed difference; the clamp stays in (.+^) alone, which is what keeps results in range.

The round-trip law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' now passes for HardWrap and for the mixed Coord [HardWrap 10, Periodic 20]. Verified on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1 via 'nix flake check' (exit 0, all checks passed).

WARNING, see sized-grid-7bp: this breaks ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs, which relied on the clamp to compute an absolute value ('max 0 (a-b) + max 0 (b-a) == |a-b|'). Its manhattan function now returns 0 for every pair, confirmed by probe. Must be patched in the same change set.

title: aoc: two call sites stop compiling once Diff is Int
description:

Built for real -- aoc's cabal.project repointed at the 0tj branch, inside aoc's nix devshell, GHC 9.12.3 -- two of the eight aoc executables that import SizedGrid fail:

  src/2017/19.hs:45   Couldn't match type 'Integer' with 'Int'
      focusedGridPosition = mempty .+^ coordFromTuple (0, toInteger col)
    The literal 0 is polymorphic and fine; 'toInteger col' is an explicit
    conversion to the type that is no longer the Diff. 'col' comes from
    elemIndex, so it is already an Int.
    FIX: drop the conversion -- coordFromTuple (0, col)

  src/2016/02.hs:16   Couldn't match type 'Int' with 'Integer' (reported at :46)
      delta :: Move -> Coord '[Integer, Integer]
    A displacement with a written-out type, which is the case the ChangeLog
    migration note already names.

build clean -- 2015/18, 2016/02, 2017/19, 2018/06, 2018/11, 2018/18, 2024/04,

title: AffineSpace (Coord cs) folds the axis list with a helper that cannot unroll: 88% of an offset loop
description:
Split out of sized-grid-0tj, which fixed the per-axis half and measured what was left.

360,000 offsets through a two-axis Coord allocate 126 MB after 0tj (was 143 MB). The same
360,000 offsets on a bare Clamped 300 axis allocate 94 KB. So ~88% of the cost is the
Coord layer, not the arithmetic, and 0tj's 11% is all the per-axis fix was ever worth on
this workload.

CAUSE. src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs, the AffineSpace (Coord cs) instance:

    Coord a .+^ Coord b =
        let helper :: All AffineSpace xs => NP I xs -> NP I (MapDiff xs) -> NP I xs
            helper Nil Nil                 = Nil
            helper (I x :* xs) (I y :* ys) = I (x .+^ y) :* helper xs ys
        in Coord $ helper a b

(.-.) has the identical shape. This is the self-recursive polymorphic fold that the
IsCoordList note in src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs documents at length: GHC does not inline
a self-recursive binding, and each call is at a shorter list, so specialising rewrites
only the outermost call and the tail runs through a generic worker that takes the
All AffineSpace dictionary at runtime. Per axis that is dictionary-peeling thunks plus the
NP rebuild. Same defect coordPosition had; moving its fold into IsCoordList as a method
took index x90000 from 27 MB to 38 bytes.

APPROACH, and the decision it needs. The proven fix is a class indexed by the axis list so
the dictionary resolves during instance resolution:

    class All AffineSpace cs => AffineCoordList cs where
        npAdd :: NP I cs -> NP I (MapDiff cs) -> NP I cs
        npSub :: NP I cs -> NP I cs -> NP I (MapDiff cs)

with instances for '[] and (x ': xs). The per-axis step needs AffineSpace x, which
IsCoordLifted does not supply, so this cannot just be another IsCoordList method -- putting
All AffineSpace cs in the *method* signature reintroduces the runtime dictionary peel that
the class was supposed to remove.

The cost is a second breaking change: AffineSpace (Coord cs)'s instance context stops
being All AffineSpace cs. Concrete call sites are unaffected, but polymorphic code that
writes All AffineSpace cs to satisfy the instance must write AffineCoordList cs instead.
In-tree that is gameOfLife/src/Main.hs (3 signatures) and README.md. ../aoc needs checking;
0tj found it builds offsets with coordFromTuple and numeric literals, which would be safe.
Making All AffineSpace cs a superclass keeps every *use* of the instance working -- it is
only the sites that discharge it that move.

VERIFY WITH the two benchmarks 0tj added to bench/Main.hs. 'four corner reads over Clamped
300x300' is the target; 'one Clamped 300 axis (no Coord)' is the control and should not
move. Follow the before/after procedure in that file's header -- do not read against the
recorded CSV.
close_reason:
Fixed by AffineCoordList, a class indexed by the axis list (commit 059f271, branch worktree-czf-affine-coord-list). 360,000 offsets through a two-axis Coord: 28.5 ms / 126 MB -> 2.02 ms / 53 B, with the bare-axis control unmoved at 2.27 -> 2.30 ms / 94 KB. Offsetting a Coord no longer allocates. Full bench suite shows no regression: 3 improve, 15 unchanged.

The predicted breaking change did not materialise in tree, and the reason is worth keeping: All AffineSpace cs is a superclass so every USE still typechecks, and instance resolution succeeds whenever the list SHAPE is known -- including cs ~ '[x, y] with x and y variable, which is how gameOfLife writes drawWorld. Only a fully polymorphic cs that actually uses (.+^) would have to change, and nothing in tree does: the All AffineSpace cs in gameOfLife and README.lhs are redundant constraints GHC already flags (sized-grid-ior). ../aoc never names the constraint.

Split out: sized-grid-135, offsetCoord still has the old shape (extend neighbourSum unmoved at 9.17 ms / 28 MB over 20,000 offsets).
Found on the way: sized-grid-4x1, two aoc call sites do not compile against 0tj's Diff = Int -- 0tj's 'aoc is unaffected' note was reasoned from a grep, not a build.

title: Coord arithmetic dominates offset-heavy read loops: 436 bytes per (.+^)
description:
Found while measuring sized-grid-up6.

The 2018/11 summed-area-table solve reads four corners per candidate square over all 90,000
positions -- 360,000 reads -- and allocates 157 MB doing it. Switching the grid from boxed to
unboxed changes that figure by nothing at all (35.2 ms boxed vs 36.4 ms unboxed, 157 MB both),
which means the cost is not the vector read. It is the coordinate.

Per corner read the loop does one (.+^) on a Coord '[Clamped 300, Clamped 300], which builds an
NP of two Ordinals, plus the list machinery around it. That is ~436 bytes per read.

For this workload that is a bigger prize than up6: up6 makes the SAT *build* 4.3x faster
(57.3 ms -> 13.3 ms) but leaves the *solve* at 35 ms untouched, so after up6 the solve is the
dominant half.

Worth investigating:
  - Does (.+^) on Coord fuse away when the offset is a loop-invariant CAF? It is not fusing here.
  - Clamped's (.+^) goes through numToOrdinal-style clamping per axis; check whether the NP
    rebuild is the cost or the clamping is.
  - An offset-by-position fast path -- compute the target position arithmetically rather than
    building an intermediate Coord -- would skip the NP entirely for the common case of a
    constant offset applied over allCoord.

Reproduce with bench-spike/ on branch worktree-up6-measure-unboxed ('SAT solve size 3' group),
or add an equivalent to bench/Main.hs.
close_reason: Diff is Int (117cd85). Per-axis (.+^) went 8.41ms/22MB -> 2.20ms/94KB across 360k offsets. The Coord-level loop only improved 11% (32.4ms/143MB -> 28.6ms/126MB): the remaining 88% is the axis-list fold in AffineSpace (Coord cs), not the arithmetic, which the issue's decomposition could not separate. Split to sized-grid-czf.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Decomposed and root-caused. Same solve loop over the same unboxed grid, each variant removing
one layer of coordinate machinery (all four variants verified to return 29, the known answer):

  Coord throughout          37.8 ms / 158 MB
  allCoord + Int corners     2.55 ms / 9.6 MB     <- (.+^) removed
  Int loops throughout       2.30 ms /  12 MB     <- allCoord removed too

So (.+^) is 35.3 ms and 148 MB of a 37.8 ms / 158 MB loop: 93 percent of the cost, and a 14.8x
ceiling on this workload. allCoord is ~0.25 ms, i.e. free -- it fuses, exactly as the note in
bench/Main.hs says.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is contained: 'Diff (Clamped n) = Integer' (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Clamped.hs:57;
Periodic.hs:87 is the same).

  Clamped a .+^ b = Clamped . unsafeOrdinal . fromInteger . max 0 .
                    min (toInteger (ordinalSize @n - 1)) $ toInteger (ordinalToInt a) + b

Per axis that is: toInteger the coord, toInteger the size bound, an Integer add, an Integer min,
an Integer max, a fromInteger back. ~5 Integer allocations per axis, 2 axes, plus the NP rebuild
-- measured at 411 bytes per (.+^) call, which is what that adds up to.

Fix: make Diff Int and keep the overflow-safety the Integer was there for. The comment on
Clamped.hs:59 justifies Integer as 'reducing to Int first could wrap a large offset into a small
one and clamp to the wrong end'. That is a real hazard but it does not need Integer, because any
offset with abs(b) >= n saturates by definition:

  Clamped a .+^ b
    | b >= sz        = maxCoord
    | b <= negate sz = zeroPosition
    | otherwise      = -- plain Int arithmetic, provably cannot overflow
    where sz = ordinalSize @n

Two Int comparisons replace the whole Integer round trip, and the saturating cases are handled
explicitly rather than relying on unbounded arithmetic.

Caveat: 'type Diff (Clamped n) = Int' is a breaking change for consumers who name Diff. Checked
../aoc: it builds offsets with coordFromTuple and numeric literals, so it is unaffected. The
Ordinal/coord law tests will need their Integer generators retyped.

WHOLE-PROGRAM IMPACT, ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs (1 SAT build + 17 solves -- part one plus sizes 1..16):
  today                    60.1 + 17x36.7 = 684 ms
  after up6 alone          15.0 + 17x37.8 = 658 ms   (1.04x)
  after 0tj alone          60.1 + 17x 2.6 = 104 ms   (6.6x)
  after both               15.0 + 17x 2.6 =  59 ms   (11.6x)

This should be done before sized-grid-up6.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Diff is now Int (commit 117cd85, branch worktree-0tj-diff-int). The fix works, but the
root cause above is wrong about where the cost was, and the correction matters more than
the fix does.

The decomposition in the previous comment compared "Coord throughout" (37.8 ms) against
"allCoord + Int corners" (2.55 ms) and attributed the whole 35.3 ms gap to (.+^). That
step removes two things at once -- the per-axis Integer arithmetic AND the fold over the
axis list that rebuilds the NP -- so it cannot say which was paying. Measured apart, on
360,000 offsets each side of the change:

  per-axis (.+^), bare Clamped 300     8.41 ms /  22 MB  ->  2.20 ms /  94 KB
  same count through a 2-axis Coord   32.4  ms / 143 MB  -> 28.6  ms / 126 MB

So the Integer really was ~all of the per-axis cost, and the per-axis cost is now zero:
94 KB across 360,000 calls, i.e. it fuses. But that was only 22 MB of the 143 MB. The
other 126 MB -- 88% -- is the fold, and it is untouched. The whole-program projection in
the previous comment (6.6x on ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs from this issue alone) does not hold;
the measured loop improved 11%.

The remaining cost is a known shape in this codebase. AffineSpace (Coord cs) does:

    Coord a .+^ Coord b =
        let helper :: All AffineSpace xs => NP I xs -> NP I (MapDiff xs) -> NP I xs
            helper Nil Nil                 = Nil
            helper (I x :* xs) (I y :* ys) = I (x .+^ y) :* helper xs ys
        in Coord $ helper a b

which is exactly the self-recursive polymorphic fold that the long note on IsCoordList in
src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs documents as unable to unroll -- GHC will not inline a
self-recursive binding, and the recursion is at a shorter list each time, so the tail
keeps going through a generic worker taking the All AffineSpace dictionary at runtime.
coordPosition had the same problem and moving its fold into IsCoordList as a method took
index x90000 from 27 MB to 38 bytes.

Filed as sized-grid-czf. It is not a drop-in repeat of the coordPosition fix: the per-axis
step needs AffineSpace x, which IsCoordLifted does not supply, so it wants its own class,
and putting that class in the instance context of AffineSpace (Coord cs) is a second
breaking change for anyone who writes All AffineSpace cs to satisfy it (gameOfLife and
README.md do, in-tree). That decision is why it is a separate issue rather than more of
this one.

bench/Main.hs now carries both benchmarks -- "four corner reads over Clamped 300x300" and
"one Clamped 300 axis (no Coord)" -- so the next person does not have to re-derive the
split. Only the gap between them says which half is paying.

title: Claim the fork: rename the package, re-own the metadata, state the design thesis
description:
The fork has diverged past any possible upstream merge, and the name it carries belongs to someone else.

FACTS
  - upstream github.com/edwardwas/sized-grid: last commit 2019-09-13
  - this fork (origin = github.com/beefyhalo/sized-grid): first Kevin commit 2025-05-09
  - 'sized-grid' on Hackage is edwardwas', maintainer ed@wastell.co.uk. This fork
    can never be released under that name.
  - divergence is not mergeable upstream anyway: GHC 9.10+ minimum,
    RequiredTypeArguments, sealed Grid constructor, Ordinal as a newtype over Int,
    gridWindows renamed to gridTiles, GHC2024.

STALE METADATA still pointing at upstream:
  sized-grid.cabal  maintainer: ed@wastell.co.uk
                    author: edwardwas
                    homepage: github.com/edwardwas/sized-grid
                    bug-reports: github.com/edwardwas/sized-grid/issues
  README.md         dead travis-ci.org/edwardwas badge (line 1)
                    Hackage badge resolving to upstream's version
                    tutorial predates the sealed Grid and RequiredTypeArguments;
                    still describes HardWrap as if the name were accurate

WORK
  1. Pick a package name.
  2. Rewrite cabal metadata to Kevin as maintainer/author, this repo as homepage
     and bug-reports. Reset version (0.1.0.0 under the new name).
  3. Decide whether the module prefix stays SizedGrid.* or follows the new name.
     Keeping it is defensible and much cheaper; renaming touches every module.
  4. README: drop both dead badges, rewrite the tutorial against the current API.
  5. Write down the design thesis, because that is what makes later API changes
     principled rather than merely permitted:
       'The coordinate type is the boundary policy. Any operation that can leave
        the space is either total because the type says how to come back, or it
        returns Maybe. Nothing clamps silently.'
     That thesis is what decides sized-grid-7gs and it is what condemns the name
     HardWrap.

Deliberately NOT blocking sized-grid-7gs: the neighbour API is designed against the
thesis either way, and 7gs should land whatever happens to the name.

title: ShrinkableGrid window constraint had x and y transposed
description:
Found while fixing sized-grid-2h0, and fixed in the same change.

src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs, instance ShrinkableGrid (c x ': cs) (c y ': as) (c z ': bs)
carried the constraint:

    z <= (x - y + 1)

where x is the number of window positions, y the source size and z the window size.
The correct relation is that a window of z at any of the x offsets must fit in y:

    (x - 1) + z <= y     i.e.   x + z <= y + 1     i.e.   z <= y - x + 1

so x and y were the wrong way round.

Why it was never noticed: the only test (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) uses x == y == 3, where
both readings collapse to 'z <= 1'. The honest case of windowing a 5-grid into three
positions of 3 (x=3, y=5, z=3) was REJECTED by the old constraint: 3 - 5 truncates to 0
in Nat, giving 'z <= 1'.

FIXED: constraint restated as 'x + z <= y + 1'. Stating it as an addition rather than a
truncating Nat subtraction also keeps it in reach of the solver.

The two remaining obligations inside 'helper' (n <= y and z <= y - n, where n is the
existential offset from asSizeProxy with n + 1 <= x) follow by linear arithmetic but
mention a truncating subtraction over an existential, which GHC cannot discharge.
ghc-typelits-natnormalise was tried and did NOT help (it does not use given <= premises
to discharge wanted <= goals), and its ghc-tcplugins-extra dependency caps at GHC <9.13,
which broke the 9.14 build. So the plugins were dropped and the facts are asserted in
SizedGrid.Internal.Type.windowFits, in the same style as the existing takeAddIsId.
Soundness rests on the instance constraint, which IS checked at every call site.

FOLLOW-UP: tests/Test/Shrink.hs still only covers x == y == 3. Add a discriminating
case (x=3, y=5, z=3) that would have caught the transposition.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:

The follow-up named in the description is DONE: tests/Test/Shrink.hs now has the discriminating case (x=3 positions, y=5 source, z=3 window) at all three offsets, which the old transposed constraint rejected at compile time. Suite is 80 tests, all passing on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1.

title: Use RequiredTypeArguments to delete Proxy from the public API
description:
GHC 9.10+ has RequiredTypeArguments ('forall n -> ...'), so the Proxy-passing style
throughout this library is now avoidable. Kevin has approved targeting 9.12/9.14
features (2026-08-09).

Current Proxy-taking API:
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:190  dropGrid  :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> Grid '[c m] x -> Grid '[c (m - n)] x
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:197  takeGrid  :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> Grid '[c n] x
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:37 sCoordSized  :: Proxy (c n) -> Proxy n
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:41 maxCoordSize :: KnownNat n => Proxy (c n) -> Integer
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:45 maxCoord     :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> c n
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:48 asSizeProxy  :: c n -> (forall m. ... => Proxy m -> x) -> x

After:
    takeGrid :: forall n -> (KnownNat n, n <= m) => Grid '[c m] x -> Grid '[c n] x
    takeGrid 3 g        -- instead of takeGrid (Proxy @3) g

    maxCoordSize :: forall (c :: Nat -> Type) n -> KnownNat n => Integer

Also removes Proxy from test and user code: tests/Main.hs is full of
'Proxy @(Periodic 10)' arguments, and ../aoc passes Proxy around too.

Related modernisation to do in the same pass:
  - default-language: GHC2024 (GHC 9.10+). GHC2024 already implies DataKinds, GADTs,
    LambdaCase, MonoLocalBinds, DerivingStrategies, RoleAnnotations,
    ExplicitNamespaces, DisambiguateRecordFields on top of GHC2021's
    ScopedTypeVariables/TypeApplications/TypeOperators/FlexibleContexts/RankNTypes.
    That deletes most of the 10-20 line LANGUAGE headers on every module.
  - TypeAbstractions ('instance ... where method @a = ...') for the IsCoord instances
    that currently need InstanceSigs + ScopedTypeVariables to bind the type variable.
  - OrPatterns (GHC 9.12) where the coord classes match several constructors alike.
  - DerivingStrategies to make the many 'deriving instance' lines in
    Coord/Periodic.hs:37-42 and Coord/HardWrap.hs:30-36 explicit about newtype vs
    stock vs anyclass.

Sequence after the plugin adoption (sized-grid-h56) so the constraint changes and the
signature changes land together rather than touching every signature twice.
notes:
GHC 9.12.3 spikes done 2026-08-11, before the work was deferred behind sized-grid-5gp. All four forms this issue needs compile:

  1. Visible Nat with constraints after the binder, on a plain function:
       takeIt :: forall m. forall n -> (KnownNat n, n <= m) => [Int] -> [Int]
  2. Passing an in-scope type variable as the required argument: 'takeIt @m k xs'.
  3. Class methods, both 'forall n -> KnownNat n => Integer' and no argument at
     all where the result type already fixes everything.
  4. A rank-2 continuation that itself takes a required type argument,
       withSize :: Int -> (forall m -> (KnownNat m, m + 1 <= 8) => String) -> String
     bound at the call site by an ordinary lambda '\m -> ...'. So asSizeProxy can
     drop its Proxy rather than keeping it in a rank-2 position.
  5. TypeAbstractions in an instance-method equation ('maxC @n = ...') works, which
     is how an instance body names a type variable once the Proxy argument is gone.

Proxy-free Nat reflection: 'fromSNat (natSing @n)' works; 'fromSNat SNat' does not
(ambiguous). Prefer natVal (Proxy @n) where Proxy is already imported for SOP.

Design decisions reached, not yet implemented:
  - maxCoordSize should stop being an IsCoord method and become a standalone
    'maxCoordSize :: forall n -> KnownNat n => Integer'. It cannot depend on c:
    asOrdinal is an Iso' (c n) (Ordinal n), so every lawful instance has exactly n
    inhabitants, and no instance overrides the default. Keeping it a method forces
    either an ambiguous c or 'maxCoordSize (type Periodic) n', because a visible
    type-constructor argument collides with the data constructor of the same name.
  - sCoordSized deletes outright; it is pure Proxy plumbing.
  - maxCoord should lose its argument entirely rather than take 'forall n ->': the
    result type c n already fixes both variables. NOTE: worktree-allcoord has since
    given maxCoord the '1 <= n' constraint this issue would also have added.
  - Rule worth stating in the ChangeLog: visible type arguments only where
    inference cannot determine them.

Blast radius check: ../aoc uses SizedGrid in 8 modules but none of takeGrid,
dropGrid, maxCoordSize, sCoordSized, asSizeProxy or maxCoord, so this break is
contained to this repo plus tests. The per-module LANGUAGE headers are also still
long (14 lines in Coord/Class.hs) despite the cabal file already setting GHC2024 --
almost all of them are now redundant and should go in the same pass.
close_reason: Done on branch worktree-required-type-args (commit d0b07ab). No public function takes a Proxy: takeGrid/dropGrid take a visible Nat, maxCoordSize became a standalone visible-forall function, maxCoord lost its argument entirely, sCoordSized is deleted, asSizeProxy is reifyCoord with a required-type-argument continuation. Minimum GHC raised to 9.10. 64 lines of redundant LANGUAGE headers removed. Clean build, zero library warnings, 129 tests plus README suite pass, no new warnings against master.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
OrPatterns, which this issue also asked for, does NOT apply anywhere here -- recording it so nobody retries.

The one site that looks like a candidate is reifyOrdinal:

    case cmpNat (Proxy @(k + 1)) (Proxy @n) of
        LTI -> func k
        EQI -> func k
        GTI -> invariantViolated ...

Two branches with an identical right-hand side. But LTI and EQI are GADT constructors of OrderingI and each brings different evidence into scope: LTI gives (k + 1) < n, EQI gives (k + 1) ~ n, and 'func k' needs k + 1 <= n derived from whichever one matched. An or-pattern has to type its right-hand side once, with no branch-specific evidence, so it cannot express this. The duplication is load-bearing.

The coord classes have no multi-constructor matches at all any more: Ordinal is a newtype since worktree-ordinal-int, and Coord matches on NP.

title: Establish a property-test baseline that would have caught the confirmed bugs
description:
The existing suite passes 62 tests while three genuine bugs sit in the library. The
laws being tested are too weak.

Gaps found:
  - tests/Test/Utils.hs:98-110 affineSpaceLaws tests only 'a .+^ zeroV == a' and
    'a .-. a == zeroV'. Both hold under HardWrap's clamping. Add the round-trip law
    'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' -- it fails on HardWrap today.
  - aesonLaws (tests/Test/Utils.hs:41-48) only round-trips valid values. Add negative
    cases: decoding a too-short / too-long array must be Nothing.
  - No test asserts the core invariant 'V.length (unGrid g) == MaxCoordSize cs'.
    Make it a property over every Grid-producing operation: tabulate, gridFromList,
    takeGrid, dropGrid, splitHigherDim, combineHigherDim, shrinkGrid, mapLowerDim,
    fmap, <*>, and FromJSON. takeGrid and splitHigherDim fail it today.
  - No Comonad law tests for FocusedGrid (extract . duplicate == id, etc.).
  - No Representable law test (tabulate . index == id) beyond the 2D case in
    tests/Main.hs:81-82.
  - No Distributive law test.
  - shrinkGrid has exactly one example-based test (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) and no
    properties.

Also: tests/Main.hs:34-38 defines Arbitrary via 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])',
which builds the entire domain for each sample -- fine at size 10, quadratic at 300.

Write these BEFORE fixing the bugs, so each fix has a failing test to turn green.

comments.text:

    (.+^) x10000, Periodic 300x300                 1.57 ms    11 MB     (157 ns/op)
    (.-.) x10000, HardWrap 100x100                  234 us   3.2 MB     (23 ns/op)
    toEnum/fromEnum x300, HardWrap 300             7.16 us    77 KB     (24 ns/op)

    tabulate 300x300   [rebuilds allCoord]         23.6 ms    93 MB
    pure 300x300       [does not]                   206 us   704 KB
    imap 300x300       [rebuilds allCoord]         17.7 ms    80 MB
    fmap 300x300       [does not]                   758 us   4.1 MB
  grid access

  indexed traversals

    itraverse 100x100                               318 us   3.4 MB
  comonad
    extract 50x50                                   154 ns   808 B
    extend neighbourSum 50x50                      5.42 ms    29 MB     (2.2 us/cell)
  collapse round trip
    collapseGrid 100x100                            163 us   2.7 MB
    gridFromList . collapseGrid 100x100             581 us   4.4 MB
  json
    toJSON 100x100                                  338 us   3.7 MB
    fromJSON . toJSON 100x100                      1.65 ms    10 MB

TWO NUMBERS THE BLOCKED ISSUES WERE WAITING FOR:

  sized-grid-uvd (allCoord rebuilt per call). The pairs are deliberately identical apart
  from whether allCoord is built:
      tabulate vs pure   23.6 ms vs 206 us   = 115x slower, 132x the allocation
      imap     vs fmap   17.7 ms vs 758 us   =  23x slower,  20x the allocation
  So allCoord is not a minor overhead on indexed traversal, it IS the cost.

standalone allCoord benchmark. 'allCoord' takes no value arguments, so at a fixed type

dereference. It reported 1.96 ns for 90,000 coordinates. Wrapping it in a NOINLINE

title: Missing API: safe neighbour offset. Users emulate it with strengthenCoord/weakenCoord through a larger grid
description:
The most-wanted operation on a bounded grid is 'move by a delta, or fail if that leaves
the grid'. The library has no such function, so users build it out of parts.

../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:63-80 -- to walk three steps in a direction on an n x n grid the
user has to widen the coordinate type to n+1, offset there, then narrow back:

    i, j, k :: Coord '[Periodic (n + 1), Periodic (n + 1)]
    i = strengthenCoord c .+^ d
    j = i .+^ d
    k = j .+^ d
    ... mapMaybe (traverse weakenCoord) ...
        \\ plusNat @n @1 \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1) \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

That is a lot of machinery to express 'neighbour, or Nothing'. It also only works
because Periodic's wrap-around at n+1 happens not to collide for small deltas -- it is
not actually a bounds check.

../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:64-66 and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:78-80 give up on the library
entirely and hand-roll:

    neighborsOf = [ toEnum nr :| toEnum nc :| EmptyCoord | ... ]

../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 uses moorePoints but must repair the result:

    experiment (filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1) g

Proposed API:

    -- fails instead of clamping or wrapping
    offsetCoord  :: Coord cs -> Diff (Coord cs) -> Maybe (Coord cs)
    neighbours   :: Coord cs -> [Coord cs]   -- Moore, excludes centre, no duplicates
    neighbours4  :: Coord cs -> [Coord cs]   -- von Neumann, excludes centre

with the boundary behaviour driven by the coord type rather than by clamping:
Periodic wraps (total), and a new 'Bounded'/'Clipped' coord returns Nothing at the
edge. Note moorePoints/vonNeumanPoints currently INCLUDE the centre, which every
observed caller then filters out -- the default is wrong.

Blocked on the HardWrap AffineSpace fix, since that is what makes the current
neighbour story incorrect.
close_reason: Done on branch worktree-neighbour-offset-7gs. offsetIsCoord (IsCoord method, bounds-check default, Periodic wraps), offsetCoord, mooreNeighbours, vonNeumannNeighbours, neighbours. moorePoints/vonNeumanPoints deleted; all five in-repo consumers migrated. Constraints drop from eight to All IsCoordLifted, and Ordinal axes now work. Clean build zero warnings, 172 tests plus README suite pass. See the issue comment for the design decisions that differ from this issue as filed.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Empirical check of the moorePoints half of sized-grid-7bp: the nubOrd workarounds at
../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 (and the commented-out ones in 2015/18 and 2018/18) must STAY.
The 0kf fix did not help them.

0kf only desugared (.-.); HardWrap's (.+^) still clamps
(src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:62-65), and moorePoints is built out of (.+^)
(src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:250-257), so every off-grid offset folds back onto the edge
cell. Measured on HardWrap 5 x HardWrap 5:

    moorePoints 1 (0,0) -> 9 results, 4 distinct   <- 5 duplicates
    moorePoints 1 (2,2) -> 9 results, 9 distinct

This is the concrete argument for the 'no duplicates' clause in the proposed
'neighbours' API above: dedup cannot be the caller's job when the clamp is what
created the duplicates.

Note vonNeumanPoints (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:275-284) was silently repaired by 0kf:
its 'min (new .-. c) (c .-. new)' picked the componentwise minimum of the two signed
diffs, which under the old clamp was 0 for every pair, so the radius filter passed
everything. It now yields -|d| and the abs makes the filter real. It still inherits the

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
DONE on branch worktree-neighbour-offset-7gs. Design recorded in
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-safe-neighbour-offset-design.md.

WHAT LANDED
  offsetIsCoord  -- new IsCoord method. Default is the bounds check; Periodic
                    overrides it to wrap and is total. (.+^) is untouched:
                    AffineSpace needs it total, and clamping is its honest
                    total form.
  offsetCoord    -- the same over a whole Coord, taking the same Diff as (.+^)
                    so it is a drop-in. Policy is read per axis.
  mooreNeighbours / vonNeumannNeighbours / neighbours (= mooreNeighbours 1)
  moorePoints and vonNeumanPoints DELETED, not deprecated.

DESIGN DECISIONS THAT DIFFER FROM THIS ISSUE AS FILED
1. No new 'Bounded'/'Clipped' coord type. HardWrap already denotes a bounded
   space; a fourth type for the same space with a different offset policy would
   be redundant. What HardWrap actually needs is a name that says 'clamps' --
   filed separately as sized-grid-7d1.
2. No 'neighbours4'. Von Neumann radius 1 is four cells in 2D but six in 3D, so
   the count is a fact about the dimension, not the operation. It is
   vonNeumannNeighbours 1.
3. Deleted rather than deprecated. The replacements change behaviour under an
   otherwise compatible signature, so the names had to go for the change to be
   a compile error instead of a silent one. Kevin confirmed breaking the API is
   fine, and raised claiming the fork as a distinct project (sized-grid-85n).

THE IMPLEMENTATION TRICK
Neighbourhoods are generated per axis, not by offsetting whole coordinates.
Each axis enumerates the values reachable within r steps and keeps each value
once, at its true step count. Consequences:
  - a cartesian product of per-axis-distinct sets is distinct, so NO duplicates
    without a nubOrd and without Ord (Coord cs);
  - the centre is the only entry whose total distance is zero, so excluding it
    needs no Eq (Coord cs);
  - on a torus the kept step count is the WRAPPED distance, which is what makes
    vonNeumannNeighbours correct on a small torus rather than accidentally
    right;
  - constraints drop from vonNeumanPoints' EIGHT to All IsCoordLifted alone,
    and they now work on Ordinal axes, which moorePoints never could (Ordinal
    has no AffineSpace instance, so All AffineSpace cs was unsatisfiable).

VERIFIED
  Clean build: library + sudoko + gameOfLife + ising-example, ZERO warnings.
  172 tests pass (up from 129) plus the README suite. sudoko still runs.
  Test-suite warnings 14 -> 6, all pre-existing; no new ones.
  Regression pinned: neighbours at a HardWrap 5 corner is exactly 3 distinct,
  where moorePoints 1 gave 9 with 4 distinct.

ALL FIVE in-repo consumers migrated, and every one had been hand-filtering the
centre back out: README tutorial, bench/Main.hs, gameOfLife, ising-example.
The benchmark now reads 8 cells not 9, so its recorded numbers move.

NOT DONE, deliberately: ../aoc migration belongs to sized-grid-bb5. Note
2024/04 must also change its grid from Periodic to the clamping coord type --
it is not a torus, it used Periodic only to make the n+1 trick work.

title: Modernise sized-grid.cabal: cabal-version 1.10, zero version bounds, missing modules, per-file LANGUAGE noise
description:
Current sized-grid.cabal problems:

  - 'cabal-version: >=1.10' (line 3). Modern baseline is 'cabal-version: 2.4' or 3.0,
    which unlocks common stanzas and the modern module syntax.

  - SizedGrid.Internal.Type is in neither exposed-modules nor other-modules.

    TypeFamilies, UndecidableInstances, PolyKinds' would delete most of the headers.

    SizedGrid/Grid/Class.hs:19-22 and tests/Test/Utils.hs:16-19 exist to support

title: Adopt ghc-typelits-natnormalise and ghc-typelits-knownnat to remove manual Nat proof plumbing
description:
The library currently discharges type-level arithmetic by hand with Data.Constraint.Nat
and, in places, unsafeCoerce.

Manual plumbing in the library:
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:61  '\\ plusNat @n @1'
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:68  '\\ leTrans @(x + 1) @n @m'
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:79  '\\ plusMinusInverse3 @1 @m \\ minusNat @m @1'
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-305  the whole AllSizedKnown class exists only to
    thread 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' through timesNat

And it leaks all the way into user code. ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:78-80 has to write:

    \\ plusNat @n @1
    \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1)
    \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

and ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:96-97 the same again via withDict. That is the library's
proof obligations showing up in a puzzle solution.

../aoc already depends on ghc-typelits-natnormalise and ghc-typelits-knownnat.
sized-grid does not. Adding

    ghc-options: -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.Normalise -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.KnownNat.Solver

discharges most 'KnownNat (n * m)', 'n <= n + 1' and 'n + 1 <= m' goals automatically.

Expected wins:
  - AllSizedKnown (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-305) likely disappears entirely, which
    simplifies the constraint on nearly every Grid function.
  - Callers stop needing KnownNat (n * n) in signatures -- cf. ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33
    'parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...'
  - The unsound axioms in SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs become unnecessary.

Caveat: plugins are a build-time dependency for *users* too if the constraints appear
in exported signatures. Measure how much of the public API simplifies before
committing. Do this before the Ordinal representation change -- it will make that
refactor much less painful.
close_reason: Merged to master (387cde5..ecd572f). Plugins adopted; the two hand-written Nat axioms (timesNat in the AllSizedKnown instance, plusNat @k @1 in reifyOrdinal) and the Data.Constraint.Nat imports are gone. Verified: nix flake check passes on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1, 283 tests pass, the plugin-free example packages still build, and sized-grid builds under ../aoc's bare-ghc912 toolchain where cabal resolves natnormalise 0.9.6 / knownnat 0.8.4 / tcplugin-api 0.19.0.0 straight from Hackage. Public API unchanged: windowFits stays an asserted axiom (needs presburger) and AllSizedKnown stays (it is plugin-free induction, not plumbing). The predicted caller-side win is NOT achievable via plugins -- they are not transitive -- and is tracked as sized-grid-k6n.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
EVIDENCE AGAINST, from trying it during the wave-02 fixes (sized-grid-2h0 / sized-grid-px9).

Both plugins were added and then REMOVED again:

1. They did not solve the problem. The wanted was 'z <= y - n' from a given 'n + 1 <= x' plus 'x + z <= y + 1'. ghc-typelits-natnormalise does not use given <= premises to discharge wanted <= goals, so the error was unchanged ('Cannot satisfy: z <= y - m'). ghc-typelits-presburger is the plugin that does this, and it is marked BROKEN in nixpkgs.

2. They break GHC 9.14. ghc-typelits-natnormalise depends on ghc-tcplugins-extra, whose bound is 'ghc >=7.10 && <9.13'; with GHC 9.14.1 the nix build fails at configure with [Cabal-8010]. Since the flake checks both 9.12.3 and 9.14.1, adopting them would have cost 9.14 support outright.

What worked instead: restate constraints as additions rather than truncating Nat subtractions where possible ('x + z <= y + 1' not 'z <= y - x + 1'), and assert the residual existential facts in SizedGrid.Internal.Type.windowFits, in the same style as the pre-existing takeAddIsId.

Recommend this issue be reconsidered or closed unless presburger becomes usable AND ghc-tcplugins-extra gains a 9.14 bound. Retest before adopting.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
RETESTED 2026-08-09 as the previous comment asked. Both blockers still stand, and one
of them is worse than 'nixpkgs has not caught up'.

1. ghc-tcplugins-extra has NO GHC 9.14 release at all -- this is upstream, not a pin
   problem. Hackage's version list tops out at 0.5, whose bound is literally
   'ghc >=7.10 && <9.13', and whose tested-with stops at GHC 9.12.1. Reproduced the
   failure end to end by building the plugin against the 9.14 package set:

       Configuring ghc-tcplugins-extra-0.5...
       Error: [Cabal-8010]
       Encountered missing or private dependencies:
           ghc >=7.10 && <9.13 (installed: 9.14.1)

   ghc-typelits-natnormalise 0.7.12 and ghc-typelits-knownnat 0.7.13 both sit on top of
   it, so all three are unavailable on 9.14 together.

2. ghc-typelits-presburger 0.7.4.2 is still meta.broken = true in nixpkgs for both
   ghc912 and ghc914. It remains the only plugin that would discharge the actual wanted
   from the wave-02 work (a '<=' goal from '<=' givens); natnormalise does not do that.

Not a stale-pin excuse: flake.lock's nixpkgs is 2026-08-06, three days old.

Also ruling out the obvious workaround, so nobody spends time on it: adopting the
plugins only for GHC < 9.13 via 'if impl(ghc < 9.13)' in the cabal file does not work
for this library. The plugins do not simplify signatures by themselves -- they let us
WRITE simpler ones. Any signature written to depend on them would then fail to compile
on 9.14, so the public API would differ by compiler. That is not acceptable for a
library, and API simplification is the entire point of this issue.

Deferring rather than closing: the plan is sound the moment upstream moves. RETEST
CONDITION, both must hold:
  - a ghc-tcplugins-extra release accepting ghc >= 9.14 (check Hackage, not just
    nixpkgs), and
  - ghc-typelits-presburger no longer marked broken in nixpkgs.
Until then sized-grid-qh9 should proceed on its own option 2.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
RETESTED 2026-08-12. The deferral's blocker is gone -- it dissolved rather than being
fixed, so the stated retest condition never triggers as written.

The condition asked for "a ghc-tcplugins-extra release accepting ghc >= 9.14". That
will not happen and no longer matters: natnormalise 0.9 and knownnat 0.8 DROPPED
ghc-tcplugins-extra and moved to ghc-tcplugin-api. Current Hackage:

  ghc-typelits-natnormalise 0.9.6   ghc >=8.8.1 && <9.15   (was 0.7.12)
  ghc-typelits-knownnat     0.8.4   ghc >=8.0.1 && <9.17   (was 0.7.13)
  ghc-tcplugin-api          0.19.0.0

ghc-tcplugins-extra is still stuck at 0.5 / 'ghc <9.13', and presburger 0.7.4.2 is
still 'ghc <9.13' and still meta.broken in nixpkgs. Neither is on the path any more.

VERIFIED, not just read off Hackage: all three build against GHC 9.14.1, and the
library + tasty suite build and pass on 9.12.3 (283 tests) and 9.14.1. 'nix flake
check' covers both.

nixpkgs' hackage snapshot still ships the 0.7.x line for both compilers, so flake.nix
pins all three with callHackageDirect. Drop those overrides once nixpkgs ships
natnormalise >= 0.9.

DONE on branch worktree-natnormalise-h56 (commit 98b9a2c): plugins enabled in
'common lang', and the two hand-written axioms removed --
'timesNat' in the AllSizedKnown instance, 'plusNat @k @1' in 'reifyOrdinal' --
along with the Data.Constraint.Nat import in both modules. Library is warning-clean.

MEASURED, since this issue said to measure before committing: the public API
simplifies by nothing. One of the three predicted wins materialised, the smallest.

  1. AllSizedKnown does NOT disappear, and should not. Its instances are what derive
     'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' inductively from per-axis KnownNats WITHOUT a
     plugin. Replacing it with a bare 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' would push the
     plugin requirement onto every downstream package writing polymorphic grid code.
     The class is load-bearing, not plumbing.

  2. "Callers stop needing KnownNat (n * n)" is NOT achievable this way, at all.
     Type-checker plugins are not transitive: sized-grid enabling them affects only
     sized-grid's modules. ../aoc solves its own constraints and does NOT enable them
     (no 'typelits' in aoc.cabal, cabal.project or flake.nix -- the premise in this
     issue's description that it already depends on them is false). Filed
     sized-grid-k6n for the actual cause: AllGridSizeKnown is a type *family*, so it
     emits 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize ...)' at the call site instead of solving it.
     That fix needs no plugin.

  3. windowFits stays. Retested by deleting it: 'Cannot satisfy: z <= y - m' and
     'Cannot satisfy: m <= y', unchanged. Still presburger's job.

Also stale in the description: the '\\ plusNat @n @1 \\ leTrans ...' plumbing cited at
../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:78-80 is already gone -- the wave-02 work removed it.

RECOMMENDATION: merge is a judgment call, and a close one. For it: two hand-written
Nat axioms and a proof-axiom dependency surface go away, and future Nat work gets
easier. Against it: three hand-pinned Hackage overrides to carry until nixpkgs
catches up, in exchange for zero public-API simplification. The concrete pain this
issue was filed about is sized-grid-k6n, which is independent of the plugins.

title: Grid is a leaky abstraction: constructor and unGrid are exported, no smart constructor
description:
src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:40-42

    newtype Grid (cs :: [Type]) a = Grid { unGrid :: V.Vector a }
      deriving (Eq, Show, Functor, Foldable, Traversable, Eq1, Show1, GHC.Generic)

Both Grid and unGrid are exported (the module has no export list at all -- every
module in the library uses an implicit 'module M where'). Anyone can build a Grid
whose vector length disagrees with MaxCoordSize cs, which is the one invariant the
library exists to enforce. The FromJSON bug and the takeGrid bug are both instances
of this.

Evidence users reach through it: ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs:31
    prefixSum1D = Grid . V.scanl1' (+) . unGrid
That is a legitimate need (prefix sums along an axis) with no API for it, so the
user bypasses the abstraction. Length-preserving uses like this are fine -- the
point is the type does not distinguish them from unsound ones.

Proposal:
  - Give every module an explicit export list.
  - Export the Grid type but not the constructor from SizedGrid.Grid.Grid.
  - Add SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe exposing UnsafeGrid/unGrid for the escape hatch,
    documented as 'you must preserve length'.
  - Add a safe 'gridFromVector :: ... => V.Vector a -> Maybe (Grid cs a)'.
  - Add the length-preserving combinators people actually want, so the escape hatch
    is rarely needed: mapAxis / scanAxis / prefix sums along a dimension
    (covers the ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs summed-area-table use directly).

Explicit export lists also let -Wmissing-export-lists be turned on, which ../aoc
already enables for its own code.
close_reason:
Grid is now abstract. Constructor and unGrid field are unexported; SizedGrid.Internal.Grid (hidden) holds the representation so SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe can be the only public route to it, and it is not re-exported by the SizedGrid umbrella.

Delivered: explicit export lists on every module, -Wmissing-export-lists on, gridVector (safe read), gridFromVector (checked build), unsafeGridFromVector (asserted build, own module), scanl1Grid (length-preserving scan).

Verified against the compiler, not by inspection: 'Grid v' -> illegal term-level use of the type constructor; 'unGrid' -> not in scope; 'g { unGrid = ... }' -> record field not in scope; unsafeGridFromVector via the umbrella import -> not in scope; via SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe -> compiles with only -XDataKinds. Public API diff (:browse SizedGrid, before vs after) is exactly +gridFromVector +gridVector +scanl1Grid and Grid becoming abstract -- nothing dropped by accident. 89 tests pass (9 new), README suite passes, library builds warning-clean.

Design change from the proposal: the escape hatch is a function, not the 'UnsafeGrid' pattern synonym. A bidirectional synonym drags the safe direction (reading) through the unsafe import, and naming a pattern synonym in an import list requires the importing module to enable PatternSynonyms.

NOT delivered, split out to sized-grid-tw3: the mapAxis/scanAxis axis-selector bullet. scanl1Grid + mapLowerDim covers the ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs case that motivated it; a general type-level axis selector is unjustified by one 2D call site. aoc migration tracked as sized-grid-bb5.

title: Ordinal's GADT representation costs a KnownNat dictionary + someNatVal allocation per arithmetic op
description:
The central performance problem.

src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:31-32

    data Ordinal m where
      Ordinal :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat m, n + 1 <= m) => Proxy n -> Ordinal m

Every Ordinal value carries a type-level Nat and its dictionary. Consequences:

  - ordinalToNum goes Proxy -> natVal -> Integer -> fromIntegral. Integer, not Int.
  - numToOrdinal (src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:50-61) calls someNatVal (allocates a
    SomeNat, builds a KnownNat dictionary via unsafeCoerce) plus cmpNat, on EVERY
    construction.
  - toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal, so enumerating an axis allocates one Nat
    dictionary per element.
  - Periodic's (<>), negateV, (.+^), (.-.) and HardWrap's equivalents all round-trip
    through numToOrdinal. A single coordinate addition allocates a type-level natural.

Observed cost in practice: ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs works on Grid '[HardWrap 300, HardWrap 300]
and iterates 'allCoord' (90,000 coords), each one an NP of two GADTs carrying dictionaries.

Proposal: make it a newtype over Int with a smart constructor.

    newtype Ordinal (m :: Nat) = UnsafeOrdinal { ordinalToInt :: Int }

The only thing the GADT buys at runtime is asSizeProxy (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:48-53),
which recovers 'Proxy m' with 'm + 1 <= n'. That is used in exactly one place
(shrinkGrid, src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:248-254). Reconstruct the evidence there via
someNatVal at that single call site instead of paying for it on every value.

Expected: coordinate arithmetic becomes machine-word Int ops; Ordinal becomes
unboxable, which unblocks the unboxed-Grid work.

Do this behind the existing _Ordinal prism / numToOrdinal / ordinalToNum API so
most call sites are unaffected. Benchmark first (see the criterion issue).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 'Make Ordinal a newtype over Int' on branch worktree-ordinal-int; 100 tests pass, zero warnings

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Dependency on sized-grid-h56 removed. h56 was retested on 2026-08-09 and deferred --
ghc-tcplugins-extra has no GHC 9.14 release on Hackage, so natnormalise and knownnat
cannot be adopted without dropping 9.14 support. Leaving this blocked on it would block
it indefinitely on an upstream event. The manual Nat plumbing in Ordinal.hs:61/68/79
therefore has to be handled by this refactor itself rather than dissolved by a plugin
first. Still blocked on sized-grid-amf, which is the right gate: benchmark before
rewriting the representation.

Also note sized-grid-j23 (fromJust in Ordinal construction) now depends on this issue --
the seven fromJust call sites collapse into one checked constructor once Ordinal is a
