title: Offset should report where it hit the edge, not just Nothing
description:
Inspiration: `Data.Manifold.WithBoundary` in the `manifolds` package.

    (.+^|) :: m -> Needle (Interior m)
          -> Either (Boundary m, Scalar (Needle (Interior m))) (Interior m)

Read it as: either you arrived in the interior, or you hit the boundary --- and here is
WHICH boundary point you hit and HOW FAR along the displacement you got.

sized-grid's `offsetCoord` (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:361-382) returns `Maybe (Coord cs)`,
which throws that information away. `Nothing` says an offset left the grid but not where
it left, not on which axis, and not how many steps succeeded first.

WHY THIS MATTERS, from a real call site

../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:64-82 wants "walk three steps in direction d from c, or tell me it
ran off". Because no such operation exists, it embeds the whole coordinate into a grid
one cell larger, offsets three times there, weakens back, and drives the type-level
arithmetic by hand:

    let i, j, k :: Coord '[Periodic (n + 1), Periodic (n + 1)]
        i = strengthenCoord c .+^ d
        j = i .+^ d
        k = j .+^ d
    ... \\ plusNat @n @1 \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1) \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

Three `Dict` entailments and a `mapMaybe (traverse weakenCoord)` for what is one ray
walk. Every raycasting, beam-tracing or line-of-sight problem has this shape.

PROPOSAL

Add the informative offset alongside the existing one:

    data OffGrid cs = OffGrid
      { lastInside  :: Coord cs   -- final coordinate still on the grid
      , stepsTaken  :: Int        -- how many whole steps succeeded
      }

    offsetCoordUpTo :: ... => Coord cs -> Needle (Coord cs)
                    -> Either (OffGrid cs) (Coord cs)

and derive a ray from it:

    coordRay :: ... => Coord cs -> Needle (Coord cs) -> [Coord cs]
    -- successive offsets until the grid runs out; infinite on an all-Periodic coord,
    -- so document that and let the caller `take`.

`offsetCoord` stays; it is `either (const Nothing) Just . offsetCoordUpTo` and remains the
right answer when the caller genuinely does not care where the edge was.

NOTE ON PERIODIC

A `Periodic` axis never fails, so on an all-`Periodic` coord `offsetCoordUpTo` is always
`Right` and `coordRay` never terminates. Mixed coords are the interesting case: the
bounded axis decides when the walk ends while the torus axis keeps wrapping, which is
already the semantics `offsetCoord` documents at Coord.hs:357-360.

DEPENDS ON the Needle change: this signature should be written against
`Needle (Coord cs)` from the start rather than against `Diff (Coord cs)` and then
migrated. If the Needle issue is rejected, this one is still worth doing against
`Diff (Coord cs)`.
design:
SHIPPED, with one deviation from the sketch above.

WHAT LANDED

    data OffGrid cs = OffGrid { lastInside :: Coord cs, stepsTaken :: Int }

    offsetCoordUpTo :: (All IsCoordLifted cs, AllDiffSame Integer cs)
                    => Int -> Coord cs -> Diff (Coord cs)
                    -> Either (OffGrid cs) (Coord cs)

    coordRay :: (All IsCoordLifted cs, AllDiffSame Integer cs)
             => Coord cs -> Diff (Coord cs) -> [Coord cs]

THE DEVIATION: offsetCoordUpTo carries a step count

The sketch had `offsetCoordUpTo :: Coord cs -> Needle (Coord cs) -> Either ...`. With
a single displacement and no count, the Left of a failed offset can only ever report
the coordinate it started from and zero steps --- it is `Maybe` again with an extra
allocation, and `stepsTaken` has nothing to count. The count is what makes the field
mean what OffGrid documents. Argument order follows `axisSteps`/`stepsWithin`/
`mooreNeighbours`: the radius-like number first.

The alternative considered and rejected: subdivide one displacement into its
primitive lattice steps (divide by the gcd of the components), so `offsetCoordUpTo`
keeps the two-argument shape and reports partial progress along a single `d`. It is
the closer analogue of manifolds' scalar, but it is surprising --- (2,3) would report
no partial progress and (2,4) would, for reasons about lattices rather than about
grids --- and every real call site wants a step budget instead.

Related decision: a step is a whole `d`, not a subdivision. On a lattice there is
nothing between `c` and `c .+^ d` unless `d` is a multiple of something shorter, so a
caller who wants the finer walk passes the finer `d`.

DIRECTION OF DEFINITION

`offsetCoord` stays the primitive; `offsetCoordUpTo` iterates it. The sketch had it
the other way (`offsetCoord = either (const Nothing) Just . offsetCoordUpTo`), but the
axes answer for a single displacement --- `offsetIsCoord` applies a whole `Diff` per
axis --- so the single offset is the honest bottom of the stack and counting steps is
iteration above it. The proposed relation is kept as a law and a property test on a
bounded, a torus and a mixed coord.

RAY SEMANTICS

`coordRay` excludes the start, for the reason the neighbourhoods exclude their centre:
every caller wants what is ahead, and `take k` then means "the first k cells along the
ray", shorter than k exactly when the grid ran out. It is infinite on an all-Periodic
coord and on a zero displacement (standing still never leaves, even on a bounded
coord); documented and tested by taking a prefix rather than guarded against. That
second case is easy to trip over --- an early property test hung on it.

WHERE lastInside IS AN EDGE

With a one-cell step, `lastInside` is on the boundary and `axisBoundaries . lastInside`
names the edge the walk met, which is the "which axis" the issue asked for. With a
wider step the walk can leave from the interior, so the guarantee is only "the last
coordinate that was inside". Both directions are pinned by tests.

ACCEPTANCE

Met, and verified out-of-tree. The aoc rewrite drops strengthenCoord, weakenCoord,
all three Dict entailments and the pad grid, switching the axes to Clamped --- which
is what the pad was simulating. Its documented examples still answer 18 and 9, and old
and new agree on all four answers over 300 random 12x12 grids. 2532/1941 could not be
produced directly: input/2024/04.txt is not in the repo. The patch is recorded in
sized-grid-4yw, to be applied WITH the merge to master (aoc builds against the main
checkout, not against a worktree branch).

NOTE FOR sized-grid-448 (coord + heading)

448 says to revisit "if the boundary-policy work makes 'what happens to a heading at an
edge' a question the library is already answering". It now half-does: a walker that
meets an edge gets back which edge and how far it got, which is the stop half of
stop/reflect/turn. Reflect and turn are still unmodelled, and there are still only two
consumers, so 448 stays parked.
acceptance_criteria: ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs can drop strengthenCoord/weakenCoord and its three Dict entailments (plusNat, leTrans, plusMonotone2) in favour of a single ray walk, and still produce 2532/1941.

title: Replace CoordDiff's per-arity tuple family with a manifolds-style Needle
description:
Inspiration: the `manifolds` package (Justus Sagemuller), `Semimanifold`'s associated
`Needle` type.

    class AdditiveGroup (Needle x) => Semimanifold x where
      type Needle x :: Type
      (.+~^) :: x -> Needle x -> x

`Needle` is an associated type, and products get theirs structurally:
`Needle (a,b) = (Needle a, Needle b)`, from the pair instance. There is no arity
ceiling and no per-arity boilerplate.

sized-grid does the opposite. src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:204-215 declares CoordDiff by hand,
one `type instance` per arity:

    type instance CoordDiff '[]              = ()
    type instance CoordDiff '[a]             = Identity (Diff a)
    type instance CoordDiff '[a, b]          = (Diff a, Diff b)
    ... up to ...
    type instance CoordDiff '[a, b, c, d, e, f] = (Diff a, ..., Diff f)

Seven instances, so six dimensions. THE CEILING IS REAL: a `Coord` of seven or more axes
has no `CoordDiff` instance, therefore `Diff (Coord cs)` is stuck, therefore no
`AffineSpace (Coord cs)` instance and no `offsetCoord`. The user can in principle add
their own `type instance` (these are open families) plus a 7-tuple, but that is an orphan
instance for something the library should supply.

The tuple encoding also forces `IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs)` into the
context of everything that offsets --- see `offsetCoord` (Coord.hs:361-368) and the
`AffineSpace (Coord cs)` instance (Coord.hs:222-226) --- which is why generics-sop
appears in consumer signatures that have no other reason to mention it.

PROPOSAL

Make the displacement coord-shaped instead of tuple-shaped:

    type Needle (Coord cs) = Coord (MapDiff cs)

`MapDiff` (Coord.hs:218-220) is already a closed, recursive family, so it needs no new
per-arity code. The payoff:

  - no arity ceiling
  - `IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs)` disappears from every signature
  - the needle inherits `:|`, `EmptyCoord`, `Show`, `Eq`, `AdditiveGroup`, `Random`
    from the existing `Coord` instances for free
  - `CoordDiff` and its seven instances are deleted outright

The `AffineSpace` helper functions at Coord.hs:234-244 and the `offsetCoord` helper at
Coord.hs:375-382 already recurse structurally over `NP I (MapDiff xs)`; they get simpler,
because `productTypeTo` / `productTypeFrom` are no longer needed at either end.

COST

Tuple literals at call sites stop working. Today ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:98 writes
`c .+^ (-1, -1)` and ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs:45 writes `mempty .+^ (0, toInteger col)`;
both would become `(-1) :| (-1) :| EmptyCoord`. That is more uniform but more verbose in
two dimensions, which is the overwhelmingly common case.

Mitigation worth evaluating as part of this issue: keep a small `IsProductType`-based
conversion available as an explicit function (say `needleFromTuple`), or supply a pattern
synonym for the 2D needle, so the ergonomic case is one short call rather than a
structural literal. Do NOT keep it as an implicit coercion in the class --- that
reintroduces the constraint this issue exists to remove.
design: Follow manifolds: the displacement type is associated and products get theirs structurally. Reuse Coord itself as the needle (Needle (Coord cs) = Coord (MapDiff cs)) rather than introducing a new product type, so all existing Coord instances and patterns apply unchanged. Keep any tuple conversion as an explicit opt-in function, never as a class constraint.
acceptance_criteria: A Coord of seven or more axes has a working AffineSpace/offset API; IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs) appears in no exported signature; the seven CoordDiff type instances are deleted; ../aoc builds against the new needle.
close_reason: Closed

title: HardWrap does not wrap, it clamps; the name has caused two bugs already
description:
'HardWrap n' clamps out-of-range values to the nearest edge. It does not wrap. 'Periodic n' is the one that wraps. The name says the opposite of what the type does, and it has been read the wrong way twice:

  sized-grid-0kf (P0)  HardWrap's (.-.) clamped negative differences to 0, breaking
                       the AffineSpace law b .+^ (a .-. b) == a for every a < b.
  sized-grid-7bp (P0)  ../aoc 2018/06 manhattan silently returned 0 as a result.

The README compounds it (README.md, coordinate-types section) by describing HardWrap
as 'like Ordinal ... but it allows a more permissive API by clamping', which is
accurate prose under an inaccurate name.

The clamping itself is not the bug and should stay: (.+^) has to be total to satisfy
AffineSpace, so clamping is its honest total approximation. sized-grid-7gs adds the
checked counterpart (offsetIsCoord, returning Nothing at the edge). What is left over
after 7gs is purely the name.

CANDIDATES
  Clamped      says exactly what (.+^) does
  Bounded      clashes with the Prelude class of that name; it also has a Bounded instance
  Clipped      fine, slightly graphics-flavoured
  Saturating   accurate and standard for arithmetic, a touch jargon-heavy

'Clamped' is the recommendation: it names the operation, has no Prelude clash, and
reads correctly at every use site ('Coord \'[Clamped 5, Clamped 5]').

Best done as part of sized-grid-85n, since that pass is already rewriting the README's
coordinate-types tutorial and is the moment breaking renames are cheapest. Filed
separately because it is a distinct decision and could be taken on its own.
acceptance_criteria: The clamping coord type has a name that describes clamping; no occurrence of 'HardWrap' remains in src, tests, examples, README or ../aoc; the suite passes.
close_reason: HardWrap renamed to Clamped throughout sized-grid (merged to master, 53b86cd) and ../aoc (7 files, 24 occurrences, uncommitted per user). Zero occurrences remain in src, tests, examples, README or ../aoc. sized-grid: library, 3 examples and benchmark build clean under -Wall; both test suites pass (172 tests + readme). aoc: 5 of 7 affected modules type-check clean; the other 2 fail on PRE-EXISTING breakages unrelated to this rename (sealed Grid constructor -> sized-grid-bb5, removed moorePoints -> sized-grid-niq), proven by checking session-start master where moorePoints survived only in a comment and Grid was already exported abstractly. ChangeLog and the dated docs/ design spec keep the old name where they are historical records.

title: Missing API: first-class axis selector for mapAxis/scanAxis
description:
Split out of sized-grid-7uj. Sealing the Grid constructor covered every bullet of that issue except the last: 'add the length-preserving combinators people actually want: mapAxis / scanAxis / prefix sums along a dimension'.

What landed instead was 'scanl1Grid', a row-major scan over the whole grid, which composes with the existing 'mapLowerDim' to give per-row scans:

    runIdentity (mapLowerDim (Identity . scanl1Grid (+)) g)

That is enough to retire the reach-through at ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs:31, but only because the summed-area-table build-up transposes between passes:

    transposeGrid . rowPrefix . transposeGrid . rowPrefix

so the 'other' axis is reached by rotating the grid rather than by naming the axis. That works for 2D and gets awkward past it -- there is no transposeGrid for an arbitrary pair of dimensions, only the 2D one.

What is missing is a way to name a dimension and act along it:

    mapAxis  :: <axis selector> -> (Grid '[c n] a -> Grid '[c n] b) -> Grid cs a -> Grid cs b
    scanAxis :: <axis selector> -> (a -> a -> a) -> Grid cs a -> Grid cs a

The design question that stopped this landing with 7uj is the selector itself: a type-level index into cs, with the machinery to prove the resulting slice type. Worth doing only if a second consumer wants it -- one 2D call site does not justify the type-level apparatus.

title: coordPosition still allocates ~550 bytes per call: dictionary plumbing, not arithmetic
description:
Follow-up from sized-grid-uvd. coordPosition is now a single Int pass (index x90000 went 75.6MB -> 54.7MB allocated), but that is still ~600 bytes per call on a two-axis coord, of which only ~56 is the benchmark's own list and thunks.

The Core (ghc -O1 -ddump-simpl on SizedGrid.Coord, worker $whelper) shows what is left, per axis per call:

  let { irred = $p1All $dAll } in
  let { $dIsCoordLifted = $p0CTuple2 (irred `cast` ...) } in
  case eq_sel ($p1IsCoordLifted $dIsCoordLifted) of ...
  integerToInt# (integerFromNatural (($p4IsCoordLifted $dIsCoordLifted) `cast` ...))
  asOrdinal ($p3IsCoordLifted $dIsCoordLifted) $fProfunctorFUN $fFunctorConst ...

So: two thunks to peel IsCoordLifted out of the All dictionary, one boxed Integer from natVal (ordinalSize goes Natural -> Integer -> Int), a call through the Iso in the IsCoord dictionary for 'c ^. asOrdinal', and two boxed Ints for the (Int, Int) the worker returns -- GHC gives (# Int, Int #), not (# Int#, Int# #).

None of it is arithmetic. All of it disappears if the function is specialised at a concrete cs.

Options:
  1. {-# INLINABLE coordPosition #-} (and on index) so consumers get a specialisation at their concrete grid type. Cheapest to try, and ../aoc uses concrete types everywhere.
  2. SPECIALIZE for the shapes the consumer actually uses -- but the library cannot know them.
  3. Get ordinalSize off Integer: GHC.TypeNats.natVal returns a Natural, and naturalToWord avoids the Integer box.
  4. Add a direct Int-level method to IsCoord so the per-axis read does not go through the Iso. Changes the class; weigh against option 1 first.

Measure with: cabal run bench:benchmarks -- --baseline bench/baseline-ghc9.12.3-aarch64-darwin.csv, watching the Allocated column on 'index x90000' (times do not transfer across sessions; allocation does).
acceptance_criteria: index x90000 allocation drops materially below 54,720,335 bytes, with the tests still passing and no new warnings
notes:
RESOLVED by option 1 (INLINABLE coordPosition). Options 2/3/4 were not needed.

Measured before/after in one session (allocation is the column that transfers;
times across the two runs drifted uniformly, as bench/Main.hs documents).

title: [minBound ..] on an Ordinal throws Maybe.fromJust: Nothing
description:
Ordinal's Enum instance defined only toEnum and fromEnum, inheriting the class
defaults for enumFrom and enumFromThen. Those defaults count up from
'fromEnum x' with no upper bound and call toEnum on each element, and Ordinal's
toEnum was 'fromJust . numToOrdinal'. So the list walked one past maxBound and
died:

    [minBound ..]        :: [Ordinal 5]   -- Maybe.fromJust: Nothing
    [maxBound, toEnum 3 ..] :: [Ordinal 5]   -- likewise, past minBound

HardWrap derives Enum from Ordinal, so it inherited the crash. The bounded
enumFromTo used everywhere in the library ('allCoordLike' uses
[minBound .. maxBound]) was never affected, which is why it went unnoticed.

The fix is the standard Bounded/Enum idiom: enumFrom stops at maxBound, and
enumFromThen picks maxBound or minBound depending on the direction of travel.
Both were defined directly over Int in the same change, which also skips the
per-element range check.

Found while rewriting Ordinal for sized-grid-upo.
acceptance_criteria: [minBound ..] and [minBound, x ..] terminate at the bound for Ordinal and HardWrap. Regression test in tests/Test/Ordinal.hs.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 'Make Ordinal a newtype over Int' on branch worktree-ordinal-int; 100 tests pass, zero warnings

title: Periodic's Enum wraps modulo n-1, so toEnum 2 :: Periodic 3 is 0
description:
src/SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:42-44

    toEnum x = Periodic $ fromJust $ numToOrdinal $
        (fromIntegral x) `mod` (maxCoordSize (Proxy @(Periodic n)))

'maxCoordSize' is natVal - 1, not natVal, so the period is one short. Every
other operation in the module uses 'maxCoordSize + 1' correctly, so it is the
only place with the off-by-one.

Consequences: fromEnum . toEnum is not the identity on the type's own range
(toEnum 4 :: Periodic 5 == 0), and toEnum 3,4,5 :: Periodic 3 gives [1,0,1]
rather than [0,1,2]. Not caught before because the coordinate enumeration path
('allCoordLike') goes through Ordinal's Enum, not Periodic's, and HardWrap's is
derived from Ordinal's.

Found while rewriting these lines for sized-grid-upo.
acceptance_criteria: fromEnum . toEnum == id on [0, n); toEnum wraps with period n. Regression test in tests/Test/Ordinal.hs.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 'Make Ordinal a newtype over Int' on branch worktree-ordinal-int; 100 tests pass, zero warnings

title: fromJust in Ordinal construction: seven call sites total only by an unchecked invariant
description:
Split out of sized-grid-0vq part (b); part (a), the four unreachable 'error' calls, is done.

'fromJust . numToOrdinal' appears in arithmetic that is total only because a mod or a
clamp happened just beforehand, which nothing checks:

  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:42, 54, 65, 74
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:44, 61
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:82        toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:83    maxCoord

Each is correct today, but the invariant lives in the reader's head, and every one of
them turns a future off-by-one into 'Maybe.fromJust: Nothing' with no indication of
which coordinate or which operation produced it.

This is deliberately NOT fixed by sprinkling error messages on the existing code. The
right fix arrives with sized-grid-upo: once Ordinal is a newtype over Int, all of these
collapse into a single 'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' whose precondition is stated once, checked
with an assert in a debug build, and free in a release build. Doing it before upo means
writing the same defensive code twice.
acceptance_criteria: No fromJust remains in src/; the single unchecked construction point documents its precondition and is assert-checked when compiled with -fno-ignore-asserts.

title: AllGridSizeKnown is a type family, so KnownNat (n*n) leaks into every consumer signature
description:
Split out of sized-grid-cpw bullet 4, with the mechanism now identified.

The library has two ways of saying 'the sizes are known' and they behave very
differently for users:

  - AllSizedKnown (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-302) is a CLASS whose instance chain is
    '(KnownNat n, AllSizedKnown as) => AllSizedKnown (c n ': as)'. GHC discharges it by
    instance resolution from 'KnownNat n' alone, and the total-size fact is handed back
    at the value level as 'sizeProof :: Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))'. Callers pay
    nothing: ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:38 gets Comonad on a FocusedGrid with only
    '(KnownNat n, 1 <= n)'.

  - AllGridSizeKnown (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:92-97) is a TYPE FAMILY that expands to
    a conjunction of KnownNat constraints, including 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)'. A type
    family cannot be discharged by instance resolution, so the whole expansion lands in
    the user's context.

That is the direct cause of the impact measured in cpw:

    ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33  parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31  parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...

Both signatures carry 'KnownNat (n * n)' purely because gridFromList is constrained by
AllGridSizeKnown rather than by AllSizedKnown. Compare the FocusedGrid signatures a few
lines below in the same files, which need nothing of the sort.

Affected API: collapseGrid, gridFromList, and the ToJSON/FromJSON instances for Grid
(Grid.hs:109, :123, :135, :153).

TWO POSSIBLE FIXES, and they should be evaluated in this order:

1. Do sized-grid-h56 first. ghc-typelits-knownnat derives 'KnownNat (n * m)' from
   'KnownNat n, KnownNat m' automatically, which makes the leaked constraint solvable
   at the call site and may make this issue disappear without touching the API.

2. If it does not, convert AllGridSizeKnown from a type family to a class in the shape
   of AllSizedKnown. The obstacle is that the four call sites recurse structurally over
   'Shape cs', and from a dictionary for 'AllGridSizeKnown (x ': xs)' there is no way to
   recover 'AllGridSizeKnown xs' -- a class dictionary cannot be run backwards through
   its own instance context. So the class would need to carry the tail's evidence
   explicitly, e.g. a method returning 'Dict (AllGridSizeKnown (Tail cs))' alongside the
   KnownNat proof. Note 'All IsCoordLifted cs' already supplies
   'KnownNat (CoordNat (Head cs))' via IsCoordLifted's superclasses, so only the
   MaxCoordSize half actually needs new machinery.
design: Prefer waiting on sized-grid-h56: a plugin fix costs one cabal line and no API churn, while the class conversion changes four exported signatures and needs new Dict plumbing. Only take option 2 if the plugins are rejected or turn out not to discharge KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs).
acceptance_criteria: ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs and ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs can drop 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' from their parse signatures and still compile.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
Superseded by sized-grid-k6n, which is closed. Same defect, filed twice: qh9 (2026-08-10) diagnosed it against src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs before that code moved to Internal/Grid.hs; k6n (2026-08-12) re-filed it after establishing that option 1 here -- 'do sized-grid-h56 first, the plugins may make it disappear' -- cannot work, because -fplugin is not transitive.

It carries it as a GridSizeProof GADT rather than a Dict, which also subsumes the SListI/Shape nil-or-cons match, so those four signatures lost that constraint too.

The literal edit to ../aoc's five signatures is sized-grid-oxb.

title: Remaining property-test gaps: Comonad/Representable/Distributive laws and O(n^2) Arbitrary
description:
Split out of sized-grid-6jd so the baseline issue can close. The baseline's blocking purpose -- write failing tests before the fixes -- is done: the three defects it gated (sized-grid-0kf, sized-grid-miz, sized-grid-2h0) each had a red test first and are now green.

Still outstanding from the original gap analysis:

  - No Comonad law tests for FocusedGrid (extract . duplicate == id,
    fmap extract . duplicate == id, duplicate . duplicate == fmap duplicate . duplicate).
  - No Representable law test (tabulate . index == id) beyond the 2D case in
    tests/Main.hs:81-82.
  - No Distributive law test.
  - shrinkGrid now has four example-based tests (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) but still no
    properties -- e.g. 'shrinkGrid at offset n == the n-th window' over arbitrary
    offsets and sizes.
  - tests/Main.hs:34-38 defines Arbitrary via 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])',
    which builds the entire domain for each sample: fine at size 10, quadratic at 300.
    Replace with a bounded 'chooseInt' + numToOrdinal.

Also worth adding now that the size invariant is enforced: extend the Test.Invariant
size property to the operations it does not yet cover (combineHigherDim, mapLowerDim,
splitGrid/combineGrid, gridWindows).

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Done on branch worktree-ryy-property-tests. 283 -> 315 tests, all passing; 'cabal build all --enable-tests --enable-benchmarks' exits 0 and both test suites (tests, readme) pass.

Every bullet is covered:

  - Comonad laws for FocusedGrid: all three, in Test.Utils.comonadLaws, run over
    '[Periodic 3, Periodic 3]' and '[Clamped 2, Periodic 3]'. Coassociativity builds a
    grid of grids of grids, so the sizes are deliberately small -- cubed cell count.
  - Representable: 'tabulate . index == id' (the direction with the payload in it; the
    existing 'index (tabulate id) c == c' compares coordinates, so a tabulate that filled
    the vector in the wrong order still passed it), plus 'index . tabulate == id' and an
    fmap/representation coherence law. Run at 2D and at 3D.
  - Distributive: four laws, incl. 'distribute . distribute == id' (a transpose done
    twice) and 'collect f == distribute . fmap f'. Run at 2D and 3D.
  - shrinkGrid properties: a 1D 'window at offset n == take 3 . drop n' and a 2D
    'window at (i,j) == the 2x2 submatrix'. The 2D one uses a 4x4 source, 2x2 window and
    3x3 offsets so the axes carry different numbers and a transposed index cannot pass by
    coincidence -- the shape the old 'z <= x - y + 1' constraint was wrong for.
  - Arbitrary: 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])' is gone. Test.Arbitrary.genOrdinal
    is 'unsafeOrdinal <$> chooseInt (0, ordinalToNum maxBound)' -- constant time, same
    uniform distribution. Deviation from the issue text: unsafeOrdinal rather than
    numToOrdinal, because chooseInt has already established the precondition and
    unsafeOrdinal's assert re-checks it in unoptimised builds anyway; it avoids a Maybe
    that cannot be Nothing. Suite still runs in 0.35s (was 0.23s).
  - Size invariant extended to the whole shape-changing API: splitGrid (outer and
    sub-grids), combineGrid, combineHigherDim, splitHigherDim, mapLowerDim, gridTiles,
    zipLowerDim, transposeGrid, shrinkGrid.

ENABLING LIBRARY CHANGE: FocusedGrid had neither Eq nor Show, so its Comonad laws could
not be written down at all. Added both as derived instances (equality is on grid AND
focus -- an Eq that ignored the focus would pass the laws without checking it) and
recorded in ChangeLog 0.3.0.0. 'comonad' and 'distributive' added to the tests stanza.

THE TESTS WERE MUTATION-CHECKED, not just observed green:
  1. duplicate := 'FocusedGrid (tabulate (const (FocusedGrid g p))) p'
     -> ONLY 'fmap extract . duplicate == id' failed. Nothing else in the suite caught it,
        which is the gap this issue was about.
  2. combineHigherDim := 'Grid v1' (drop the second operand)
     -> the new 'combineHigherDim sums the outer axis' failed, alongside two pre-existing.
  3. axes swapped in the 2D window property
     -> that property failed alone, confirming it is genuinely orientation-sensitive.
Each mutation was reverted and the suite re-run green.

title: Add a compile-fail test harness for the size invariants
description:
Wave 02 (sized-grid-2h0) tightened takeGrid/dropGrid/splitHigherDim so that misuse is a type error rather than a silently wrong Grid. That is the right outcome, but it means the regression tests for it cannot live in the tasty suite: 'takeGrid (Proxy @9)' of a 3-grid no longer compiles, so it cannot be asserted at runtime.

Right now those cases survive only as comments in tests/Test/Invariant.hs. Nothing would catch a future loosening of the signatures.

Options:
  - 'should-not-typecheck' (uses deferred type errors; brittle)
  - a cabal 'build-type: Custom' / shell script compiling snippets and asserting failure
  - GHC's own '-fdefer-type-errors' plus a runtime catch of TypeError
  - doctest with ':t' expectations

Cases to cover:
  - takeGrid (Proxy @9) :: Grid '[Ordinal 3] -> Grid '[Ordinal 9]   (needs 9 <= 3)
  - dropGrid (Proxy @9) on a 3-grid
  - splitHigherDim remainder annotated as anything other than x - y
  - ShrinkableGrid with a window that does not fit (x + z > y + 1)

title: Constraint hygiene: redundant superclass constraints leak into every user signature
description:
Several instances demand more than they use, and the noise propagates to callers.

  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Focused.hs:26-32 and :36-42
    Comonad and ComonadStore for FocusedGrid both require 'All Monoid cs, All Semigroup cs'.
    The bodies only use index and tabulate, which need AllSizedKnown + All IsCoordLifted.
    The Monoid/Semigroup constraints appear unnecessary -- verify and drop them.

  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:70
        instance (All Eq cs, All Ord cs) => Ord (Coord cs)
    Eq is a superclass of Ord, but 'All' does not propagate superclasses, so callers
    must write both. Fixable with a Dict-based entailment helper.

  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:1 sets -Wno-redundant-constraints for the entire module,
    which is why these are not already flagged. Remove the blanket flag; the whole
    point of -Wredundant-constraints (already in ghc-options) is to catch this.

  - AllSizedKnown vs AllGridSizeKnown vs All IsCoordLifted are three overlapping ways
    of saying 'the sizes are known'. ToJSON (Grid) uses AllGridSizeKnown + SListI while
    FromJSON (Grid) uses All IsCoordLifted, for what should be dual operations.
    Consolidate to one constraint synonym.

Measured impact on users: ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33 and ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31 both
have to carry 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' in signatures purely to satisfy AllSizedKnown.
The typelits-plugin issue would remove most of this; this issue covers what remains.
close_reason: Focused.hs Comonad/ComonadStore shed All Monoid/All Semigroup; blanket -Wno-redundant-constraints removed from Grid/Grid.hs with two dead constraints deleted and four soundness constraints kept behind a new 'requiring' helper so the warning stays on. Ord (Coord cs) proved unfixable (GHC cannot induct over AllF for a type variable) and is now documented in place. Constraint consolidation split out as sized-grid-qh9, blocked on h56. Verified on ghc 9.12.3 and 9.14.1.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Worked through all four bullets. Two fixed, one proved impossible, one split out.

BULLET 1 -- Focused.hs Comonad/ComonadStore. FIXED. 'All Monoid cs, All Semigroup cs'
were unnecessary on both instances, exactly as suspected: the bodies only use index and
tabulate, which need nothing beyond Grid's Representable instance. Dropped from both;
library, both test suites and both nix GHCs still build. This was the worst of the four
because Comonad is the only reason to reach for a FocusedGrid at all, so every consumer
was repeating the noise.

BULLET 3 -- the blanket -Wno-redundant-constraints on Grid/Grid.hs:1. FIXED, flag gone.
With it removed GHC reported five constraints, and they split two ways:

  Genuinely dead, removed:
    combineHigherDim  IsCoord c
    splitHigherDim    IsCoord c, KnownNat x
  IsCoord buys nothing here -- a coord's size comes from CoordNat on the IsCoordLifted
  instance, not from IsCoord, so the class could not have justified the n + m or x - y
  in those result types even in principle.

  Load-bearing, KEPT:
    dropGrid/takeGrid  n <= m
    splitHigherDim     y <= x
    gridWindows        Mod (CoordNat big) (CoordNat small) ~ 0
  These are the soundness constraints added in 7bdd829. -Wredundant-constraints only
  looks at whether the BODY uses a constraint, and these are consumed by the caller's
  types, so it flags them wrongly. Drop 'y <= x' from splitHigherDim, for instance, and
  splitting a 5-grid at 9 returns a first component typed 'c 9' holding 5 elements.

  To keep the warning switched on rather than trading one blanket suppression for
  another, those four now name what they are enforcing via a new internal helper,
  SizedGrid.Internal.Type.requiring:

      takeGrid p (Grid v) = requiring @(n <= m) $ Grid $ V.take (natVal p) v

  It is 'id' with a constraint, so it is free at runtime, and it turns an invisible
  contract into a visible one. (Its body has to build a Dict rather than being plain
  'id', or the helper's own constraint gets reported as redundant.) Note it is NOT
  named 'contract' -- Data.Constraint already exports that and Grid.hs imports it.

BULLET 2 -- 'instance (All Eq cs, All Ord cs) => Ord (Coord cs)'. NOT FIXABLE. The
issue proposes a Dict-based entailment helper; that does not work here. Tried it, GHC
9.12.3 says:

    Could not deduce 'AllF Eq cs' arising from a superclass required to satisfy
    'All Eq cs', arising from the superclasses of an instance declaration
    from the context: All Ord cs

'All c cs' expands to the type family 'AllF c cs', and reducing 'AllF Eq cs' from
'AllF Ord cs' needs induction over cs, which the solver will not do for a type variable
-- it works only for concrete lists. Data.SOP.Dict.mapAll can produce the evidence, but
as a VALUE, and superclass evidence for an instance must be discharged at declaration
time where no value is in scope. Both constraints stay; the instance now carries a
comment saying why, so nobody retries this.

BULLET 4 -- consolidating AllSizedKnown / AllGridSizeKnown / All IsCoordLifted. SPLIT
OUT as sized-grid-qh9, blocked on sized-grid-h56.

  First, part of this bullet is stale: ToJSON and FromJSON for Grid are already aligned
  (Grid.hs:135 and :153 both use AllGridSizeKnown + SListI). 7bdd829 fixed that.

  Second, the three constraints are not actually redundant with each other -- they say
  different things, and collapsing them to one synonym would over-constrain APIs like
  'Applicative (Grid cs)' that only need the total size. The real defect is narrower and
  I found the mechanism: AllSizedKnown is a CLASS, so instance resolution discharges it
  from 'KnownNat n' per element and hands back the total size as a value-level Dict,
  whereas AllGridSizeKnown is a TYPE FAMILY that expands into the user's context. That
  single difference is what puts 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' in ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33 and
  ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31 while the FocusedGrid signatures right below them stay clean.
  Details and the two candidate fixes are in sized-grid-qh9.

title: Replace dead Travis CI and stale nix pin with GitHub Actions
description:
.travis.yml (9.4 KB) targets travis-ci.org, which shut down. There is no working CI.

Also removed/replaced as part of the flake work:
  - nixpkgs-version.json pinned nixpkgs-channels at a 2018-09-05 revision. That repo
    is archived. The file is now unused -- delete it.
  - shell.nix used to be '(import ./default.nix).env' but default.nix does not exist
    in the repo, so nix-shell was simply broken. Now a flake-compat shim.

Wanted: .github/workflows/ci.yml that
  - runs 'nix flake check' (builds the library + tests + haddock on ghc912)
  - runs a matrix of 'cabal build --enable-tests' over GHC 9.6 / 9.8 / 9.10 / 9.12
    via haskell-actions/setup, to keep the declared bounds honest
  - builds the example sub-projects once they compile again (see the examples issue)
  - caches ~/.cabal and dist-newstyle

Then delete .travis.yml.
notes:
From sized-grid-s25 (2026-08-10): the three examples are now packages of the root cabal.project, so any CI job that runs 'cabal build all' picks them up and they cannot rot again -- no per-example CI step is needed. Two constraints for whatever workflow this issue adds:

  - gameOfLife and ising-example depend on gloss, which pulls OpenGLRaw/GLURaw/OpenGL/GLUT. These build unaided on macOS (verified on aarch64-darwin, GHC 9.12.3) because the frameworks come from the SDK, but a Linux runner needs system packages first: libgl1-mesa-dev, libglu1-mesa-dev and freeglut3-dev before 'cabal build all'. Without them GLUT fails to configure and the whole 'build all' fails, taking the library check down with it.

The flake was deliberately left alone: mkPackage callCabal2nix's sized-grid.cabal only, so 'nix flake check' still covers just the library and its tests. Adding the examples there would put a gloss/GLUT build in front of every 'nix flake check'.

title: SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs is dead code containing an unsound axiom
description:
src/SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs is imported by nothing. Verified:

    grep -rn 'SizedGrid.Internal' src tests sudoko/src gameOfLife/src ising-example/src
    -> only its own module header and module declaration

It is also absent from both 'exposed-modules' and 'other-modules' in sized-grid.cabal,
so cabal does not know about it at all (it would be omitted from an sdist).

Its contents are worth deleting rather than wiring up:

  - takeAddIsId (line 52-53):
        takeAddIsId :: forall m . Dict (((m - 1) + 1) ~ m)
        takeAddIsId = unsafeCoerce (Dict :: Dict (a ~ a))
    This is false at m = 0. It is an unsound axiom obtained by unsafeCoerce, and if
    anything ever imported it, it could be used to derive nonsense.

  - sLessThan (line 41-49) fabricates an SBool (n <=? m) via unsafeCoerce off a
    runtime Integer comparison. Sound in practice but the comment on 'magic'
    (line 55, 58) literally says 'don't really understand it' / 'Also don't understand'.

  - SBool/SBoolI duplicate what singletons or Data.Type.Bool already provide.

Action: delete the module. If a KnownNat-subtraction proof is needed later,
ghc-typelits-natnormalise supplies it soundly (see the plugin issue).

Also fix the cabal file to list every module -- the same audit should confirm nothing
else is missing.
close_reason: Module is no longer dead (windowFits + requiring are imported by Grid/Grid.hs) and is listed in the cabal file, so it was trimmed rather than deleted: removed the six unused definitions including the unsound takeAddIsId axiom, and closed the export list to (windowFits, requiring). Module audit clean; cabal check now warning-free; sdist builds and tests from scratch.

title: Grid is boxed-vector only; no unboxed/storable representation for numeric grids
description:
src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:40 hardcodes Data.Vector (boxed).

For the numeric workloads this library is aimed at, that is the wrong default:
  - ising-example/src/Main.hs is a Monte Carlo spin simulation
  - gameOfLife/src/Main.hs is a cellular automaton
  - ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs builds a 300x300 Int summed-area table
All of these want Data.Vector.Unboxed and get boxed Ints with a pointer chase each.

The complication: Functor/Applicative/Monad/Representable/Traversable all require the
element type to be unconstrained, so Grid cannot simply switch to Unboxed.

Options:
  1. Parameterise over the vector type:
       newtype GridOf v (cs :: [Type]) a = GridOf (v a)
       type Grid = GridOf V.Vector
     Keep the current instances for the boxed version; give the unboxed version the
     instances it can support (Foldable-like ops via a Vector.Generic constraint,
     no Functor). Costs an extra type parameter in every signature.
  2. Leave Grid boxed and add a separate SizedGrid.Grid.Unboxed with a monomorphic
     API (map/zipWith/fold/index taking Unbox constraints). Less elegant, far less
     disruptive, and covers the actual use cases.

Recommend option 2 first -- it is additive and non-breaking. Revisit 1 only if the
duplication becomes painful.

Prerequisite either way: benchmarks, so the win is measured rather than assumed.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Baseline landed (sized-grid-amf). Relevant figure for the unboxed-Grid case: a 300x300
Grid of Int costs 93 MB of allocation to build via tabulate and 72 MB to read back via
index over allCoord, against a true payload under 1 MB. Most of that is Ordinal and
Coord boxing rather than the vector itself, so sized-grid-upo should land first --
switching the vector to unboxed cannot help while every element access still constructs
a boxed Coord. Benchmarks to watch: 'tabulate 300x300', 'index x90000' and 'fmap
300x300' in bench/Main.hs.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Unblocked in principle by the sized-grid-upo work: Ordinal is now a newtype over
Int, so a Coord's components are machine words rather than GADTs carrying
dictionaries. That was the stated prerequisite for an unboxed or storable Grid.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Measure-first spike (bench-spike/, branch worktree-up6-measure-unboxed, ghc 9.12.3 aarch64-darwin).
Minimal UGrid over Data.Vector.Unboxed vs the real Grid, same shapes, same workloads, both
sides through coordPosition/allCoord so the coord machinery cancels.

  operation (300x300 Int)   boxed              unboxed            delta
  tabulate                  14.2 ms / 20 MB    1.90 ms / 9.6 MB   7.5x faster
  index x90000              765 us  / 26 B     751 us  / 41 B     none
  map then sum              1.52 ms / 4.1 MB   92.5 us / 18 B     16x faster
  foldl'                    312 us             86.8 us            3.6x faster
  row prefix scanl1         1.68 ms / 4.2 MB   845 us  / 5.5 MB   2x faster
  transpose                 14.6 ms / 18 MB    2.24 ms / 9.6 MB   6.5x faster
  SAT build (2018/11)       57.3 ms / 64 MB    13.3 ms / 40 MB    4.3x faster
  SAT solve, 360k reads     35.2 ms / 157 MB   36.4 ms / 157 MB   none

Conclusion: the win is real but it is NOT where up6's description assumed. It is entirely in
BULK operations that touch the vector wholesale (3.6x-16x). Per-coordinate access wins exactly
nothing -- 'index' and the SAT solve are identical to within noise, because their cost is the
Coord arithmetic and not the vector read.

That settles the API shape: an unboxed grid wants map/zipWith/fold/scanl1/tabulate/transpose,
and there is no point optimising an indexed read path.

Caveat on the fmap row: part of that 16x is fusion U.map/U.foldl' get and the derived
Functor/Foldable on Grid do not, so read the SAT build (4.3x on a whole real workload) as the
honest headline. Caveat on index: both benchmarks walk row-major, which is the prefetch-friendly
best case for boxed. The consumer's real access patterns are also near-sequential, so this is
representative rather than flattering.

Separate finding, filed as its own issue: the SAT solve burns 157 MB for 360,000 reads (~436 B
per read) and that is all coordinate arithmetic ((.+^) over allCoord), not the grid.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
From the sized-grid-zzj evaluation (closed): if this lands on vector-sized rather than raw Data.Vector.Unboxed, note that vector-sized 1.6.1 indexes with Data.Finite's Integer-backed alias, not an Int-backed one:

    index (Vector v) (Finite i) = v `VG.unsafeIndex` fromIntegral i
    generate f = Vector (VG.generate i (f . Finite . fromIntegral))

So an Ordinal -> Finite conversion at that boundary allocates an Integer per index, and that cost is inherent to vector-sized rather than to Ordinal -- switching Ordinal's representation would not avoid it. Given the spike above already showed per-coordinate access wins nothing and the whole win is in bulk operations, the cheap route is to keep the bulk API off the index path entirely (map/zipWith/fold/scanl1/tabulate/transpose over the underlying vector) and not route reads through Finite at all. Raw Data.Vector.Unboxed, as the spike used, sidesteps the question.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Ordering: sized-grid-0tj should land first. Decomposing the solve loop showed (.+^) is 93% of
it, with a 14.8x ceiling, against up6's 4.3x on the build. On ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs as a whole
(1 build + 17 solves) up6 alone is 1.04x, 0tj alone is 6.6x, both together 11.6x. up6 is still
worth doing -- it is most of what is left once 0tj lands -- but it is the second half, not the
first. Full numbers and root cause on sized-grid-0tj.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Follow-up: evaluated forking vector-sized. Recommendation is DON'T -- and don't
depend on it either. Use raw Data.Vector.Unboxed, as the spike above did.

Maintenance status (checked 2026-08-13): dormant, not dead.
  - Last commit 2024-02-01 (~2.5 years ago); not archived; 6 open issues, 2 open PRs.
  - Last release 1.6.1 uploaded 2024-02-07 by koz_ross, not the author (expipiplus1).
  - Last FEATURE release was 1.6.0, January 2022 (~4.5 years ago). The two releases
    since were life support -- bounds bumps and foldl' future-proofing contributed by
    Bodigrim, i.e. an ecosystem caretaker keeping it compiling.
  - tested-with maxes at GHC 9.2.1.
  - BUT it builds fine on GHC 9.12.3 -- verified by compiling against it; 1.6.1 is
    already in the nix GHC package set. The presburger lesson recorded in
    sized-grid.cabal is that the risk is a dep that stops BUILDING on a GHC we need,
    not one that stops adding features. vector-sized is not there.

The strong version of the fork idea does work, and deserves credit: fork it and swap
Finite n for our own Ordinal n, and finite-typelits disappears along with the
KnownIntegral/Limited constraint wall documented in sized-grid-zzj. That would give an
Int-backed index under plain KnownNat, the vocabulary the rest of the library speaks.
So the fork genuinely can solve the representation problem.

It fails on three other counts:

1. It duplicates a size proof we already have. Grid is
   'newtype Grid (cs :: [Type]) a = Grid (V.Vector a)' -- a flat vector carrying our
   own type-level size machinery (cs, Coord, Ordinal, AllGridSizeKnown). A type-level
   size tag IS vector-sized's whole value proposition. Adopting it puts a
   Vector (product-of-cs) a inside a Grid cs a: two independent size proofs to keep in
   agreement, plus the product constraint relating them. AllGridSizeKnown already
   carries KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs) as a superclass, and sized-grid-oxb is open work
   to REMOVE a KnownNat (n * n) from signatures. Same direction as the finite-typelits
   migration, same reason to decline.

2. Cost: 9,521 lines across 12 modules, with deps on adjunctions, comonad,
   distributive, binary and primitive -- owned forever, on our GHC upgrade schedule.
   Ordinal.hs is ~200 lines.

3. It buys nothing the spike above needs. All measured wins (7.5x tabulate, 16x
   map/sum, 4.3x SAT build) are bulk operations over the underlying vector, which never
   touch an index type. The spike also found per-coordinate access wins nothing --
   and the indexed read path is exactly the surface vector-sized would provide.

A fork would be justified if we wanted to EXPOSE a size-tagged vector in the public
API, or if vector-sized broke on a GHC we need and upstream stayed silent. Neither
holds. If the second ever does, the proportionate fix is a bounds-bump PR or a Hackage
revision -- which is precisely what the last two releases were.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Re-priced after sized-grid-czf landed, on the real consumer rather than by projection.

WHOLE PROGRAM, ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs (1 SAT build + 17 solves), same binary shape
both sides, aoc's nix devshell, GHC 9.12.3 aarch64-darwin:

  against master (pre-0tj, pre-czf)   0.72 s   2.91 GB allocated   MUT 0.645 s
  against 0tj + czf                   0.28 s   1.07 GB allocated   MUT 0.207 s

2.6x end to end. That is the coordinate work finished; up6 is what is left.

WHERE THE REMAINING 207 ms GOES. Split by re-benchmarking the two halves of that
program separately (scratch package, code copied unchanged from 11.hs):

  makeSAT 300x300, the build          78.5 ms
  solve 3, one solve of 360k offsets   8.02 ms
  solve 3 with 'corners' hoisted       4.12 ms

1 build + 17 solves = 78.5 + 17x8.02 = 215 ms, against 207 ms measured. The model
is the program.

So the shares are: build 36 percent, solves 64 percent. And of a solve, only
~2.0 ms is the library's offset path (the 'four corner reads' benchmark, now
2.02 ms / 53 B per 360,000 offsets) -- the other ~6 ms is the caller rebuilding
its four-element 'corners' list inside squareSum, once per position, 90,000 times
a solve. Hoisting it halves the solve. Filed separately.

WHAT up6 IS NOW WORTH HERE. The build is bulk operations over the whole grid --
tabulate, scanl1Grid, mapLowerDim, transposeGrid -- which is exactly the shape
the spike above measured at 4.3x for the SAT build and 7.5x for tabulate. At
that ratio the build goes 78.5 -> ~18 ms, i.e. ~28 percent off the program, 1.4x.
It does NOT help the solves: the spike measured per-coordinate index reads as
unchanged (765 us boxed vs 751 us unboxed), and this split confirms the solve
half is caller-side list building rather than element access.

So: still worth doing, and now the largest library-side item left for this
workload, but as a 1.4x on the build half and not a rewrite of the hot loop. The
stronger cases remain ising-example and gameOfLife, which are bulk map/zip over
numeric grids end to end -- 16x on map/sum in the spike -- rather than
offset-and-read like 11.hs.

Recommendation unchanged: option 2, an additive SizedGrid.Grid.Unboxed with a
monomorphic API, non-breaking.

title: Partial functions throughout: fromJust in coord arithmetic, error in complete pattern matches
description:
Two separate problems.

(a) 'error' calls that are genuinely unreachable but are there only because GHC cannot
see the ':|' pattern synonym is complete:
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:255   shrinkGrid _ = error "Impossible pattern in shrinkGrid"
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:319       weakenCoord _ = error "Unreachable pattern in weakenCoord"
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:333       strengthenCoord _ = error "Unreachable pattern in strengthenCoord"
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:203       error "Error in adding Coord. Should be unreachable"

Fix: add '{-# COMPLETE (:|) #-}' and '{-# COMPLETE EmptyCoord #-}' pragmas next to the
pattern synonyms in src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:53-58. The dead equations then delete
cleanly and the warnings stay on. Cheap, zero risk, removes four error calls.

(b) 'fromJust . numToOrdinal' in arithmetic that is only total because of an invariant
GHC is not checking:
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:48, 59, 70, 80
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:45, 61
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:82  (toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal)

These are 'correct' given mod/clamp, but they are also the hot path (see the Ordinal
representation issue) and they turn any future off-by-one into a crash with no
context. Switching Ordinal to a newtype over Int lets these become a single
'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' whose precondition is stated once and checked with an assert
in a debug build.
close_reason: Part (a) complete: COMPLETE pragmas removed three unreachable error equations, and the fourth was removed by switching Coord's AffineSpace instance to productTypeFrom/productTypeTo (a COMPLETE pragma cannot help there, evidence in comments). No 'error' remains in src/. Part (b), the fromJust sites, split out as sized-grid-j23 blocked on sized-grid-upo.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
PART (a) DONE -- all four unreachable 'error' calls are gone. 'grep -rn "error \"" src/'
now returns nothing.

Three of them went exactly as this issue predicted. Added next to the pattern synonyms
in Coord.hs:

    {-# COMPLETE (:|) #-}
    {-# COMPLETE EmptyCoord #-}

after which the fallback equations in weakenCoord (Coord.hs), strengthenCoord
(Coord.hs) and shrinkGrid (Grid/Grid.hs) delete cleanly with -Wincomplete-patterns
still on. Cheap and zero risk, as advertised.

The fourth needed a different fix, and the one this issue proposed would not have
worked. In the AffineSpace instance for Coord, ('.+^') matched 'from b' against
'SOP (SOP.Z bs)' with an error fallback. No COMPLETE pragma helps there -- the scrutinee
is a generics-sop sum, and although 'IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs)' does
give 'Code (CoordDiff cs) ~ \'[MapDiff cs]' as a given, GHC will not reduce the type
family application far enough to see that the 'SOP.S' arm would have to hold an
'NS I \'[]'. Confirmed by deleting the fallback and getting:

    warning: [-Wincomplete-patterns] Pattern match(es) are non-exhaustive
      Patterns of type 'SOP I (Code (CoordDiff cs))' not matched: SOP (SOP.S _)

Fixed by not building the sum in the first place: generics-sop exports
'productTypeFrom :: IsProductType a xs => a -> NP I xs' and its inverse 'productTypeTo',
which go straight to and from the NP. ('.+^') and ('.-.') now use those instead of the
generic 'from'/'to' plus manual SOP/Z plumbing. Shorter, and there is no unreachable
branch left to write.

PART (b), the fromJust call sites, is SPLIT OUT as sized-grid-j23, which depends on
sized-grid-upo. Reason: this issue already says the real fix is a single
'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' with an asserted precondition, and that only exists once Ordinal
is a newtype over Int. Patching the seven sites now means writing the same defensive
code twice. There are eight, incidentally, not seven -- Coord/Class.hs:83 maxCoord was
missed in the original list.

Verified: cabal build all warning-free, both suites green.

title: The other IsCoord defaults still read their KnownNat as a run-time Natural
description:
sized-grid-bw8 fixed offsetByPosition with a one-line INLINE: the checked offset went from 56.4 ms / 199 MB to 6.85 ms / 35 MB, and in the Core the per-axis call went from $w$coffsetIsCoord main81 ds3 ww2 to an inline ># x (-# 299# y1). The same shape is still in its siblings in src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs.

WHAT IS LEFT. The Core of SizedGrid.Coord.Class still shows integerToInt# (integerFromNatural ($dKnownNat cast ...)) in:
  1. axisBoundaryByPosition, the default for axisBoundaryIsCoord.
  2. the default axisDistanceIsCoord.
Both read ordinalSize @n out of the method's KnownNat dictionary, for the same structural reason bw8 documents: IsCoord is indexed by c alone, so n arrives on the method rather than through the instance.

A third, different in kind: Periodic's own offsetIsCoord override is 'Just (c .+^ d)'. Its body folds, because AffineSpace (Periodic n) takes KnownNat n from its instance context --- but the method is still an out-of-line call taking the dictionary, so a Periodic call site does not get what Clamped now gets.

WHY NOT DONE IN bw8. bw8 was scoped to offsetByPosition, and nothing in bench/Main.hs reaches onBoundary or axisDistance. An INLINE on them could not have been measured, and this codebase does not take unmeasured performance changes --- the whole point of the before/after procedure in that file's header.

APPROACH. Add the benchmarks first: an onBoundary sweep over Clamped 300x300 and an axisDistance one, both shaped like checkedCornerReads so the displacement depends on an argument and cannot be floated into a CAF. Then the same one-line INLINE, verified in the Core rather than assumed.

ORDERING with sized-grid-5uq. axisSteps calls both offsetIsCoord and axisDistanceIsCoord, so part of this may land there instead. bw8 already took 'extend neighbourSum 50x50' from 8.88 ms / 28 MB to 7.01 ms / 25 MB without touching the neighbourhood fold, purely through the offsetIsCoord axisSteps calls.
notes:
APPROACH CHANGED BY sized-grid-knm (commit 66d50ee).

knm expected to fix a quadratic scan and instead found that the caller being out
of line was the whole cost: one INLINE on axisSteps, 6.51 ms / 22 MB -> 2.12 ms /
9.9 MB. So for this issue, check the caller before the class default.

Concretely: this issue's plan is an INLINE on axisBoundaryByPosition and on the
axisDistanceIsCoord default. But onBoundary and axisDistance are themselves free
functions over IsCoordList, and if they are out of line the pragma on the default
buys nothing at a call site -- which is exactly the trap knm's premise fell into.
Dump the Core of the new benchmarks first and see which frame the dictionary is
still being passed at.

The benchmark plan in this issue stands unchanged; nothing in bench/Main.hs
reaches onBoundary or axisDistance, and knm did not add anything that does.

The Periodic offsetIsCoord override noted here is now the more interesting half:
Clamped's path folds completely at a concrete axis after knm, so a Periodic call
site is where the remaining gap is, and it is measurable as soon as a Periodic
neighbourhood benchmark exists.

title: No test checks that coord operations produce in-range values
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while adding the asOrdinal Iso laws (sized-grid-6p4).

The new 'asOrdinal lands in [0, n)' property quantifies over 'arbitrary', and
Test.Arbitrary's genOrdinal draws through unsafeOrdinal at an already-reduced
index. So every coord the property sees is in range BEFORE asOrdinal is applied:
it cannot catch a coord that an operation built out of range.

The operations that build coords with unsafeOrdinal, each of which is asserting
its own precondition rather than checking it:

  Clamped  Semigroup   unsafeOrdinal (min (ordinalSize @n - 1) (a + b))
  Clamped  .+^         unsafeOrdinal (fromInteger (max 0 (min (size-1) (a + b))))
  Periodic Semigroup   unsafeOrdinal ((a + b) `mod` ordinalSize @n)
  Periodic toEnum      unsafeOrdinal (x `mod` ordinalSize @n)

unsafeOrdinal does check, with Control.Exception.assert -- but cabal builds the
test suite at -O1, where GHC compiles assertions away. So in the suite as it
runs today that check is not live, and a wrong mod or a wrong clamp would
produce an Ordinal outside [0, n) that nothing rejects. It would then index a
vector out of bounds, or silently read the wrong cell.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, not exclusive:
  1. Add 'ghc-options: -fno-ignore-asserts' to the tests component, which makes
     every existing property that exercises these operations into a range check
     for free. Cheapest by far.
  2. State it directly as a property: for arbitrary a, b, the results of (<>),
     (.+^) and toEnum all satisfy 0 <= ordinalToInt < ordinalSize.

Option 1 is the one with leverage -- the suite already generates a great deal of
Semigroup and AffineSpace traffic, and none of it is currently range-checked.
