title: Evaluate finite-typelits' Finite against the hand-rolled Ordinal
description:
`SizedGrid.Ordinal.Ordinal` is a hand-rolled `Fin`:

    newtype Ordinal (m :: Nat) = UnsafeOrdinal { ordinalToInt :: Int }
    type role Ordinal nominal

`finite-typelits` provides the same abstraction as `Data.Finite.Finite`, and the
overlap is not approximate -- it exports `weaken`, `strengthen`, `shift`,
`unshift`, `finites`, `modulo`, `packFinite` and `getFinite`, which line up
almost name-for-name with `weakenOrdinal`, `strengthenOrdinal`, `allOrdinal`,
`numToOrdinal` and `ordinalToInt`.

This is an evaluation, not a planned migration. Decide it once and write the
answer down, because "should this just be `Finite`?" is the sort of question
that resurfaces every time someone new reads `Ordinal.hs`.

The reason it is worth asking now rather than never: sized-grid-up6 wants an
unboxed/storable grid representation, and the obvious way to get one is
`vector-sized`, which is built on `Finite`. If the library is ever going to meet
`Finite` at its boundary, better to know deliberately than to end up converting
at every call.

The strong argument against, which the evaluation has to clear first:
`Data.Finite.Finite` is `Integer`-backed, and this library deliberately uses
`Int` because the sizes index a `Data.Vector.Vector` and have to fit in an `Int`
anyway (see the comment on `ordinalSize`). Swapping a machine int for a heap
`Integer` in the type that every coordinate is built from would fight the
allocation work in sized-grid-92z and the coordposition benchmarks head-on.

One thing to check before concluding, because it may dissolve that objection:
the Hackage docs for current `finite-typelits` present `Finite` as an alias of a
more general underlying type parameterised by its representation, which suggests
an `Int`-backed variant may be available. Settle that first -- the whole decision
turns on it.

Also confirm what `Ordinal`'s `nominal` role costs to reproduce. That role
annotation is load-bearing here (its comment explains that a phantom role makes
`coerce :: Ordinal 9 -> Ordinal 3` typecheck), and the Hackage docs do not state
a role for `Finite`. If `Finite`'s role is phantom or representational, adopting
it would silently give away an invariant this library is careful about, and that
alone settles the question.
design:
DECISION: keep Ordinal. Do not adopt finite-typelits.

Evaluated against finite-typelits 0.2.1.0 (current on Hackage, x-revision 2),
GHC 9.12.3, with both project plugins (Normalise, KnownNat.Solver) active.

== The two pre-registered objections both DISSOLVE ==

1. Representation width: NOT a blocker. Data.Finite.Integral exports the
   general type, `newtype Finite a (n :: Nat) = Finite a`, with a real
   `instance SaneIntegral Int`. `Finite Int n` is a newtype over Int -- byte
   for byte what `Ordinal m` is. `Data.Finite`'s `Finite n` is merely
   `Finite Integer n`. The Integer concern applies only to the alias.

2. Role: NOT a blocker. Data/Finite/Internal/Integral.hs declares
   `type role Finite nominal nominal` -- nominal in BOTH parameters.
   Verified: `coerce :: Finite Int 9 -> Finite Int 3` is rejected
   ("Couldn't match type '9' with '3'"). Finite guards the size index
   exactly as carefully as Ordinal's `type role Ordinal nominal` does.

So the reason recorded here is neither of the two the issue anticipated.
Two facts found while checking settle it the other way.

== The decisive reason: KnownIntegral does not compose with KnownNat ==

Finite's operations are constrained by `KnownIntegral a n`, not `KnownNat n`,
and the two do not connect in either direction:

  - `KnownNat n` does NOT give `KnownIntegral Int n`. Verified; the error is
    "Cannot satisfy: n <= 9223372036854775807". The lone instance is
    `(SaneIntegral a, Limited a n, KnownNat n) => KnownIntegral a n`, and
    `Limited Int n` reduces to `n <= maxBound::Int`. Neither natnormalise nor
    knownnat discharges that for a polymorphic n -- and polymorphic n is the
    entire point of this library. (Concrete literals are fine; that is not
    the case that matters.)

  - `KnownIntegral Int n` does NOT give `KnownNat n` back. It is an instance
    context, not a superclass, so it never propagates backwards. `natVal` is
    unavailable under it -- and `ordinalSize` calls `natVal`.

A ported signature therefore has to carry BOTH constraints (verified: that
version compiles). That is 88 KnownNat occurrences across 6 modules in src/,
and it does not stop at the library boundary -- aoc's call sites inherit it.
It also pushes directly against sized-grid-oxb, which is work to REMOVE a
constraint from signatures.

The escape hatch, `withIntegral`, recovers KnownNat at runtime via
`someNatVal` + `unsafeCoerce Refl`. Commit 99b4332 removed this library's last
unsafeCoerce. Reintroducing one per call site to satisfy a dependency is a
strictly worse trade than the ~200 lines Ordinal.hs costs to own.

== The motivating premise (up6 / vector-sized) is false ==

The stated reason to ask now was that vector-sized is built on Finite, so the
library will meet Finite at its boundary anyway. It will not meet the Int one.
vector-sized 1.6.1 indexes with Data.Finite's Integer-backed alias:

    index (Vector v) (Finite i) = v `VG.unsafeIndex` fromIntegral i
    generate f = Vector (VG.generate i (f . Finite . fromIntegral))

Adopting `Finite Int n` would remove NO conversion at that boundary -- you
would convert `Finite Int n` -> `Finite Integer n` exactly as you would
convert an Ordinal. Adopting the Integer-backed alias to genuinely match is
the allocation regression this issue feared, head-on against sized-grid-92z.
Either way sized-grid-up6 gains nothing here.

== Consequence for up6 ==

If up6 adopts vector-sized, it needs a small ordinalToFinite/finiteToOrdinal
pair at the boundary, and that conversion allocates an Integer per index
regardless of what Ordinal is. That is a cost of vector-sized, not of Ordinal,
and it should be weighed inside up6.

Do not reopen on representation width or role; both were checked and both are
fine. Reopen only if finite-typelits makes KnownIntegral derivable from
KnownNat for polymorphic n (i.e. Limited becomes discharged automatically),
which would remove the entire cost above.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision recorded on this issue: either Ordinal is replaced by Finite with benchmarks showing no allocation regression, or the issue is closed with the specific reason (representation width and/or role) so the question is not reopened.
close_reason: Evaluated and declined: keep Ordinal. Both anticipated objections (Integer representation, role) turned out NOT to apply -- finite-typelits has an Int-backed Finite and declares 'type role Finite nominal nominal'. It fails on constraint composition instead: KnownIntegral Int n is not implied by KnownNat n (needs undischargeable 'n <= maxBound::Int' for polymorphic n) and does not imply it back, so ported signatures need both constraints across 88 KnownNat sites in src/ plus aoc's call sites, or a per-call-site unsafeCoerce via withIntegral. Separately, the motivating premise is false: vector-sized indexes with the Integer-backed alias, so adopting Finite Int removes no conversion at that boundary. Full analysis in the design field.

title: Head and Tail are exported type families with no remaining user
description:
sized-grid-k6n replaced the AllGridSizeKnown type family with a class, and the class matches on 'c n ': as' directly. Head and Tail (src/SizedGrid/Internal/Grid.hs:199-205) existed only to write that family and its four call sites; nothing in the library mentions them now.

They are still exported from SizedGrid.Internal.Grid and re-exported from SizedGrid.Grid.Grid, so they remain public API. ../aoc does not use them (checked: no match for Head or Tail as whole words under aoc/src).

Decide: keep them as generic type-level list utilities, or drop them as surface that exists for no reason. This belongs with the API pass in sized-grid-85n rather than on its own, since removing an exported name is the kind of break that wants to land with the others.

title: coordSpaceSize has coordPosition's defect: sList induction does not unroll
description:
Found while closing sized-grid-6ou, which fixed the same defect in coordPosition.

coordSpaceSize (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs) folds over the axis list with sList induction:

    coordSpaceSize = case sList :: SList cs of
        SNil         -> 1
        SCons @xs @x -> ordinalSize @(CoordNat x) * coordSpaceSize @xs

That is polymorphic recursion, which is exactly what sized-grid-6ou established GHC will not unroll. Verified in Core at a concrete three-axis list: it does NOT constant-fold to 7000, it builds the IsCoordList dictionary chain as a value and calls a generic worker.

    lvl8 = $fIsCoordList: lvl1 lvl7
    sz = case $wcoordSpaceSize lvl8 of ww { __DEFAULT -> I# ww }

Reproduce by compiling 'coordSpaceSize @(quote)[Clamped 50, Clamped 20, Clamped 7]' against the library with -O2 -ddump-simpl.

WHY THIS IS LOWER PRIORITY THAN 6ou WAS: coordSpaceSize is called once per tabulate (to size the vector up front), not once per cell, so it is not multiplied by 90,000 the way coordPosition was. tabulate 300x300 already improved 47 MB -> 20 MB from the 6ou fix alone.

THE FIX IS NOW MECHANICAL, because IsCoordList already exists and is already in coordSpaceSize's context. Add a second method:

    class (IsCoordListF cs, All IsCoordLifted cs) => IsCoordList cs where
      sizeAndPosition :: NP I cs -> (Int, Int)
      coordListSize :: Int

    instance IsCoordList '[] where coordListSize = 1
    instance (IsCoordLifted x, IsCoordList xs) => IsCoordList (x ': xs) where
      coordListSize = ordinalSize @(CoordNat x) * coordListSize @xs

then coordSpaceSize = coordListSize, and it constant-folds like sizeAndPosition does. Note coordListSize duplicates the first component of sizeAndPosition; that is deliberate, because coordSpaceSize has no coordinate to fold over and sizeAndPosition needs a single pass. Do not try to derive one from the other.

MEASURE WITH: 'tabulate 300x300' and 'pure 300x300' in the bench suite, and confirm the Core folds to a literal, which is the real check.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Do NOT reach for cpara_SList here, even though it looks like the general answer.

Measured while answering whether sList induction has a general fix. cpara_SList does unroll in isolation -- a coordSpaceSize-shaped fold through it constant-folds to I# 7000# at '[Clamped 50, Clamped 20, Clamped 7] -- but only where the axis list is concrete, which needs INLINE all the way down to such a site. Tried on coordPosition against the real benchmarks it was a regression: 584 B a call on extract 50x50 and 50 MB on index x90000, against 320 B / 27 MB before any fix, because the polymorphic instance methods it is called from (index, gridIndex) give the inliner nowhere concrete to land.

coordSpaceSize is called from tabulate, which is equally polymorphic, so expect the same trap. Add the coordListSize method to IsCoordList as described in the description; that resolves at specialisation rather than depending on the inliner.

title: coordPosition still costs 320 bytes per call after specialisation
description:
Follow-up from sized-grid-0vl, which took coordPosition from 608 to 320 bytes per call by exposing its unfolding with INLINABLE so consumers specialise at a concrete cs.

320 bytes for what should be a couple of multiplies and adds is still 40 words, so something in the path is not melting away even when the All dictionary is statically known.

The measurement to work against is 'extract 50x50' in the benchmark suite: it is a single coordPosition call and nothing else, so its Allocated column IS the per-call cost, with no traversal or list machinery mixed in. It reads 320 bytes at the commit that closed sized-grid-0vl (was 608).

  cabal run bench:benchmarks -- -p '$0 ~ /extract 50x50/'

Options 3 and 4 from sized-grid-0vl are still on the table and were never tried,
because option 1 alone cleared that issue's acceptance criterion:

  3. Get ordinalSize off Integer. It is 'fromInteger $ natVal (Proxy @m)', and
     GHC.TypeNats.natVal returns a Natural, so naturalToWord avoids the Integer
     box. At a concrete size this should constant-fold anyway, which is a reason
     to check whether it is really what is left before changing it.
  4. Add a direct Int-level method to IsCoord so the per-axis read does not go
     through the asOrdinal Iso. Changes the class, so weigh it last.

Worth doing first: dump Core for a concrete two-axis call and find out what the
40 words actually are, rather than guessing. 'cabal build' will not re-dump on a
ghc-options change alone -- the module has to actually change for the dump to
regenerate.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (Core, not guesswork). coordPosition's fold was a where-helper, which makes it polymorphically recursive over the axis list: it calls itself at a shorter list. GHC specialises the outermost call and STOPS, leaving one shared worker $whelper that takes the All IsCoordLifted dictionary at run time. So the INLINABLE from sized-grid-0vl did work -- for axis one only, which constant-folded. Every axis after it paid, per axis: two thunks to peel the dictionary ($p1All, $p0CTuple2), integerFromNatural for ordinalSize, asOrdinal applied through $fProfunctorFUN/$fFunctorConst, and two boxed I#. That is the 40 words. The comment then at Coord.hs:324 named those exact costs but concluded INLINABLE removed them.

MEASURED OPTIONS (2-axis, coord-construction baseline subtracted; the 328 B here cross-validates the benchmark's 320 B):
  current                                    328 B
  option 3 alone (ordinalSize off Integer)   336 B  -- NO WIN, ruled out
  options 3+4 (+ direct Int read)            216 B  -- 34% off, option 4 does all the work
  class-based induction                       32 B  -- 90% off
  -fpolymorphic-specialisation -fspecialise-aggressively  328 B -- worker byte-for-byte identical

Also ruled out with Core: lifting the helper to a top-level INLINABLE function (identical), and routing the fold through generics-sop's cpara_SList (its cons is a function ARGUMENT, so the per-axis dictionary stays a run-time value). Only an instance method resolves it.

FIX SHIPPED: new class IsCoordList cs in SizedGrid.Coord.Class carrying the fold as method sizeAndPosition, with All IsCoordLifted cs as a superclass and a IsCoordListF type-family superclass so that IsCoordList (x ': xs) hands back IsCoordList xs (the shape generics-sop gives its own All, needed or every local induction over the axis list stops typechecking). Replaced All IsCoordLifted with IsCoordList throughout: a rename, not an added obligation.

RESULT: coordPosition at '[Clamped 50, Clamped 50] compiles to +# (*# x 50#) y, zero allocation.
  extract 50x50   320 B -> 0 B,     92.6 ns -> 11.0 ns
  index x90000     27 MB -> 38 B,   8.05 ms -> 753 us
  ifoldl' 300x300  30 MB -> 2.7 MB, 8.24 ms -> 1.03 ms
  imap 300x300     35 MB -> 7.6 MB, 15.1 ms -> 4.86 ms
  tabulate 300x300 47 MB -> 20 MB,  24.6 ms -> 14.1 ms
  extend neighbourSum 32 MB -> 26 MB
  Nothing regressed; pure/fmap/itraverse/collapseGrid/coord arithmetic all unchanged.

CONSUMER IMPACT: none. ../aoc works at '[Clamped n, Clamped n] with (KnownNat n, 1 <= n), and IsCoordList is discharged there by instance resolution exactly as All IsCoordLifted was; verified by typechecking aoc's verbatim signatures against the new API. (A full ../aoc build is blocked by a pre-existing unrelated failure: hmatrix needs blas/lapack C libs.)

FOLLOW-UP: sized-grid-92z, coordSpaceSize has the identical defect via sList induction.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the closing notes above, found while answering "is there a general fix to sList induction?".

The notes say cpara_SList does not unroll "because its cons is a function ARGUMENT, so the per-axis dictionary stays a run-time value". That explanation is WRONG. An eliminator whose step is a function argument unrolls fine; a clone of cpara_SList, and generics-sop's own, both constant-fold a coordSpaceSize-shaped fold to a literal (I# 7000#) at a concrete three-axis list.

What actually separated the two cases in the original experiment was INLINE vs INLINABLE on the WRAPPER. The failing test marked the wrapper INLINABLE, so GHC specialised it rather than inlining it, and specialisation lambda-lifts the higher-rank step into a shared worker that keeps the per-axis dictionary at run time. Flip that one pragma to INLINE and the identical code unrolls. Verified both directions, one variable at a time.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and is the real reason the class was the right fix:

1. The old where-helper was SELF-RECURSIVE, and that can never unroll -- GHC does not inline a self-recursive binding. Verified: the original body with INLINE instead of INLINABLE still leaves 'Rec { $whelper ... }' with the runtime dictionary. So the defect was real and no pragma could have fixed it.

2. cpara_SList + INLINE unrolls in isolation but is a REGRESSION in this library, measured on the real benchmarks:

     extract 50x50   320 B before -> 0 B (class) -> 584 B (cpara+INLINE)
     index x90000     27 MB before -> 34 B (class) -> 50 MB (cpara+INLINE)

   Because coordPosition is called from polymorphic instance methods (index on Representable, gridIndex on IsGrid), INLINE splices the eliminator into a body where cs is still a type variable and nothing can resolve, so it builds the closure chain per call. Unrolling through an eliminator needs INLINE all the way down to a concrete call site, and this library's call path does not provide one.

3. A class method has no such dependency on the inliner: the instance chain resolves whenever the DICTIONARY is known, which happens at specialisation, not only at inlining.

Source Haddock and ChangeLog have been corrected to say this. Consequence for sized-grid-92z: do NOT rewrite coordSpaceSize through cpara_SList; add a method to IsCoordList as that issue already proposes.

title: ChangeLog claims GHC 9.8 support, but base >=4.20 and tested-with both say 9.10
description:
ChangeLog.md (0.3.0.0, near the end) says:

    * Builds with GHC 9.8 through 9.14 via a nix flake

Two things in sized-grid.cabal contradict it:

    line 91  base >=4.20 && <4.23     -- base 4.20 ships with GHC 9.10, not 9.8
    line 29  tested-with: GHC ==9.10.1 || ==9.12.3 || ==9.14.1

GHC 9.8 ships base 4.19, which the bound excludes, so the package cannot build
there at all. Nothing is broken -- the code and the cabal file agree with each
other, and only the prose is wrong.

Noticed while adding coordDistance (sized-grid-lcl): the new code uses foldl'
from Prelude, which is base 4.20+. That is fine under the real bound and would
NOT have been fine under the claimed one, which is what prompted the check.

FIX: either correct the sentence to 9.10, or decide 9.8 is meant to be
supported and lower the base bound plus add it to tested-with. The flake is the
place to confirm which GHCs are actually wired up.

title: AllSizedKnown restates evidence All IsCoordLifted already determines
description:
Inspiration: the witness pattern in the `manifolds` package. `SemimanifoldWitness` and
`PseudoAffineWitness` exist, in Hackage's words, to "reify constraints to avoid requiring
UndecidableSuperclasses" --- inductive evidence packaged as a VALUE in the class, because
a superclass cannot carry it.

sized-grid states the same fact twice, as two separate obligations:

  - `All IsCoordLifted cs` gives, per axis, `KnownNat (CoordNat x)` and
    `x ~ CoordContainer x (CoordNat x)` (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:111-119).
  - `AllSizedKnown cs` (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:487-498) gives
    `Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))`.

The second is DETERMINED by the first: `MaxCoordSize` is the product of the per-axis
nats, and `AllSizedKnown`'s own instance body is nothing but that induction with
`timesNat` at each step. So it is derivable evidence being demanded as a separate class.

SCOPE CORRECTION --- READ THIS BEFORE ESTIMATING THE PAYOFF

This is NOT a consumer-ergonomics win, and an earlier framing of it overstated the case.
sized-grid-qh9 already established that for a CONCRETE `cs` the class is discharged by
instance resolution from `KnownNat n` alone and callers pay nothing. The cost lands only
where `cs` is a type variable, i.e. the library's own signatures and polymorphic helpers:

    src/            19 occurrences (grep -rn AllSizedKnown src/)
    tests/Main.hs:86,154        alongside `All IsCoordLifted cs`
    gameOfLife/src/Main.hs:59,152

and gameOfLife is the clearest case, because it lists BOTH halves of the same fact:

       , KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)
       , AllSizedKnown cs

`AllSizedKnown cs` supplies exactly that `KnownNat` as a `Dict`, so the two lines are
redundant with each other.

PROPOSAL

Replace the class with a function that produces the evidence from the dictionary the
caller already has:

    sizeProof :: forall cs. All IsCoordLifted cs => Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))

by induction on `sList`, `timesNat @(CoordNat x) @(MaxCoordSize xs)` at each step.

PREREQUISITE: `MaxCoordSize` (Coord.hs:256-258) currently matches on the SHAPE `c n`:

    MaxCoordSize ((c n) ': cs) = n GHC.* (MaxCoordSize cs)

which will not reduce for an abstract axis type. Restate it via the projection so it
reduces from `IsCoordLifted` alone:

    MaxCoordSize (c ': cs) = CoordNat c GHC.* MaxCoordSize cs

RISKS

  - Widens some signatures from `AllSizedKnown cs` to `All IsCoordLifted cs`, which
    additionally demands `1 <= n` per axis. Affects the sites that use `AllSizedKnown`
    ALONE today: `gridFromVector` (Internal/Grid.hs:112), `Applicative (Grid cs)`
    (:139), `Arbitrary1` (tests/Test/Arbitrary.hs:38). Probably fine --- a zero-width
    axis makes `MaxCoordSize` zero and the grid empty --- but it must be checked rather
    than assumed.
  - `sizeProof` becomes a per-call induction over `sList`. See the recorded memory
    `sized-grid-slist-from-all-dict`: getting `sList` from an `All c xs` dictionary is
    NOT free, it goes through `cpara_SList`. Here the fold is over DIMENSIONS (at most a
    handful), not cells, and produces a `Dict` GHC can float --- but the benchmark suite
    should confirm `pure`/`tabulate` do not regress, since `Applicative (Grid cs)` calls
    it on every `pure`.

RELATED: sized-grid-qh9 covers the mirror-image problem for `AllGridSizeKnown` (a type
family, so it DOES leak to consumers). These two should be designed together --- qh9's
option 2 proposes converting `AllGridSizeKnown` INTO the shape of `AllSizedKnown`, while
this issue proposes dissolving `AllSizedKnown` into a function. Resolve the disagreement
before either is implemented.
design: Witness pattern from manifolds: derivable inductive evidence should be a value produced from a dictionary the caller already holds, not a separate class the caller must satisfy. Prerequisite is restating MaxCoordSize via CoordNat so it reduces for an abstract axis type. Must be reconciled with sized-grid-qh9, which proposes moving AllGridSizeKnown INTO the shape this issue proposes dissolving.
acceptance_criteria: AllSizedKnown is gone from src/; tests/Main.hs and gameOfLife/src/Main.hs each drop a constraint without gaining one; bench shows no regression in pure/tabulate.

title: tests/Main.hs still threads Proxy tokens through six law-helper functions
description:
Left over from sized-grid-all (2026-08-11), deliberately.

tests/Test/Utils.hs exports six helpers that all take a 'Proxy' as a type token:

    semigroupLaws, monoidLaws, additiveGroupLaws, affineSpaceLaws, aesonLaws,
    isCoordLaws

and tests/Main.hs calls them in groups sharing one binding:

    let p = Proxy @(Periodic 10)
    in [ semigroupLaws p, monoidLaws p, ..., isCoordLaws p ]

sized-grid-all removed Proxy from the *library* API but left these alone. The
reason: converting one of six siblings would have been worse than converting
none, since they share the 'p' binding at every call site, and converting all
six is a separate refactor with its own churn.

These are also a different use of Proxy from the one that issue was about. They
carry a *type* to test, not a size, and the visible-forall form is awkward for
types whose constructors share their name -- 'twoDimensionalCoordTests (type
(Coord '[HardWrap 10, Periodic 20]))' needs the 'type' keyword because 'Coord'
is also a data constructor. The natural fix here is AllowAmbiguousTypes plus a
type application ('isCoordLaws @Periodic @10'), not a required type argument.
acceptance_criteria: The six helpers take their type by application rather than by Proxy, tests/Main.hs no longer binds 'p', and the suite still passes with no new warnings.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text: Scope grew on 2026-08-12 (sized-grid-ryy): Test.Utils now has NINE Proxy-threaded law helpers, not six. The three new ones -- comonadLaws, representableLaws, distributiveLaws -- were deliberately written in the existing Proxy style rather than the type-application style this issue proposes, so that the conversion is one uniform change instead of leaving the module in two styles at once. Nothing here is harder as a result; there is just more of it.

title: Missing API: sliding windows over a grid (stride 1), distinct from gridTiles
description:
gridTiles (renamed from gridWindows in sized-grid-61o) cuts a grid into DISJOINT tiles: an Ordinal 9 axis tiled by Ordinal 3 gives 3 tiles. The name it used to have promised the other operation -- a sliding window of size 3 at each of the 7 offsets -- and that operation still does not exist.

The primitive is already there: shrinkGrid (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs) extracts a sub-grid at a coordinate offset, and the ShrinkableGrid constraint 'x + z <= y + 1' already states exactly 'a window of z taken at any of the x offsets fits inside a source of y'. A sliding-window function is shrinkGrid mapped over all offsets.

Wanted:
    gridWindows :: ... => Grid (big ': rest) a -> [Grid (small ': rest) a]
      -- CoordNat big - CoordNat small + 1 results, stride 1, overlapping

Consumers: summed-area / convolution style problems. ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs builds 3x3 and NxN sums by hand over a prefix-sum grid, which is what this would replace.

Left out of sized-grid-61o deliberately: that issue was the P0 hang, and adding a new operation is not needed to fix it.
acceptance_criteria: gridWindows returns CoordNat big - CoordNat small + 1 overlapping sub-grids at stride 1; a size larger than the source is a type error; property test that every window equals the corresponding shrinkGrid at that offset.

title: Speculative: coord + heading (FibreBundle/ParallelTransporting)
description:
Inspiration: `Data.Manifold.FibreBundle` in the `manifolds` package.

    data FibreBundle b f = FibreBundle { baseSpace :: b, fibreSpace :: f }
    type TangentBundle m = FibreBundle m (Needle m)

A tangent bundle is a point paired with a direction at that point, and the associated
`ParallelTransporting` class answers the question "as I move along the space, what happens
to my heading?"

sized-grid has half of this already. `FocusedGrid cs a` (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Focused.hs:18)
is a grid paired with a position --- a pointed structure. What is missing is the heading.

Consumers hand-roll it:

    ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs:71   type State n = (FocusedGrid '[HardWrap n, HardWrap n] Cell, Dir)
    ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs:63   shift :: Dir -> Coord ... -> Coord ...
    ../aoc/src/2017/19.hs      the same pattern again, on a hand-rolled Map-based grid

WHAT THE ANALOGY BUYS

The interesting content is not the pair --- anyone can write a pair --- it is
`ParallelTransporting`: the boundary policy should decide what happens to the heading
when a walker meets an edge. On a `Periodic` axis the heading is unchanged and the walker
wraps. On a `HardWrap` axis there is a genuine choice the library could name: stop,
reflect, or turn. Today every consumer re-decides that inline, and ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs
gets it right only by ACCIDENT --- it relies on `HardWrap`'s `(.+^)` clamping so that
walking off the keypad edge silently returns the walker to where it was:

    move fg c = let next = seeks (.+^ delta c) fg
                in if isNothing $ extract next then fg else next -- It's a "wall", stay put

That works, but nothing in the types says it should, and the clamp is documented
elsewhere in this library as the behaviour callers must not rely on.

STATUS: SPECULATIVE, FILED FOR THE RECORD

This is the weakest-justified item in the set and is deliberately backlogged. Two real
consumers is not a strong enough signal to add a type, and the design question --- is a
heading a `Needle`, a unit step, or a per-axis sign? --- is unresolved.

DO NOT START THIS before the Needle issue lands. A heading is most naturally
`Needle (Coord cs)` restricted to unit steps, so the representation question is
downstream of how needles are represented at all.

Revisit if a third consumer wants it, or if the boundary-policy work makes
"what happens to a heading at an edge" a question the library is already answering.
design: Deliberately backlogged. The valuable part is not the pair but ParallelTransporting: letting the axis's boundary policy decide what a heading does at an edge (Periodic wraps unchanged; HardWrap must choose stop/reflect/turn). Blocked on the Needle representation, since a heading is most naturally a unit Needle.
acceptance_criteria: Not scheduled. Revisit if a third consumer wants it or if the boundary work makes edge-heading semantics a question the library already answers.

value: ghc-typelits-natnormalise does NOT chain '<=' givens. Probed directly on GHC 9.12.3 (sized-grid-wrc): it fails on a bare 'a <= b, b <= c => a <= c'. It DOES cancel constants from both sides ('m + 1 + z <= y + 1' gives 'm + z <= y'). So when a Nat goal will not solve, the fix is usually to restate it as linear addition rather than truncating subtraction, and to name the transitivity/monotonicity steps explicitly with plusMonotone1 and leTrans from Data.Constraint.Nat -- 'constraints' is already a dependency. Reach for a solver plugin last: ghc-typelits-presburger would work but is bounded 'ghc <9.13' on ghc-tcplugins-extra 0.5 with no 9.14 branch, so it costs GHC 9.14 support.

sized-grid: IsCoord's 'asOrdinal :: Iso' (c n) (Ordinal n)' carries NO KnownNat n, and that makes two of its four laws unfalsifiable. An instance cannot build an Ordinal n at all -- unsafeOrdinal and numToOrdinal both need the size -- so the only ordinal it can return is the one it was handed. Consequences, established by mutation testing on 2026-08-13 (sized-grid-6p4): 'view asOrdinal . review asOrdinal == id' and 'asOrdinal lands in [0,n)' CANNOT fail for any instance; they are the law written down, not tests. The one direction with teeth is 'review asOrdinal . view asOrdinal == id', which a non-injective instance (an extra field dropped on the way out and invented on the way back) does falsify. 'reifyCoord agrees with asOrdinal' also has teeth, because reifyCoord does have KnownNat n and Ordinal overrides it. Do not add more asOrdinal round-trip properties expecting them to catch anything.

aoc's FocusedGrid call sites: 'experiment f w' centres f on 'pos w', NOT on any Coord you happen to have in scope. The correct idiom when you hold a separate coord is 'experiment neighbours (seek coord g)'; the idiom when the grid is already refocused (inside extend) is 'experiment neighbours fg'. aoc/src/2025/04.hs got this wrong for months -- 'experiment (filter (/= coord) . ...) g' looks like it centres on coord but centres on the constant parse-time focus (0,0). Grep aoc for 'experiment' before trusting any neighbourhood result; 2015/18 and 2018/18 are the correct pattern.

sized-grid: a Grid traversal restricted to some subset of cells needs no library function. Grid cs is TraversableWithIndex (Coord cs) (src/SizedGrid/Internal/Grid.hs:192), so the index is the coordinate and any Coord predicate filters it: 'itraversed . indices (not . onBoundary)' is the interior as a read-write IndexedTraversal, 'indices isCorner' the corners. Check for this composition before adding a named traversal to the Grid API.

sized-grid indexed traversals: 'V.fromList allCoord' inside V.zipWith FUSES -- the coordinate list is streamed, never materialised, and dies in the nursery. Replacing it with anything the simplifier cannot see through (a vector from a recursive function, or the same list under V.fromListN) forces 90,000 live coordinates: measured +23% allocation and +59% time on imap 300x300, and ifoldl' copying went from 48KB to 18MB. Do not 'fix' allCoord in imap/ifoldMap/itraverse. tabulate is the exception -- its result is a vector regardless, so V.fromListN there is a small win.

sized-grid displacements: Diff (Coord cs) is Coord (MapDiff cs) -- a coord again, one Diff per axis -- NOT a tuple. Changed 2026-08-12 by sized-grid-iet, which deleted the CoordDiff family and its seven per-arity instances. Consequences: (1) there is no arity ceiling any more; CoordDiff stopped at six axes, so a 7-axis Coord had no Diff, no AffineSpace and no offsetCoord. (2) IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs) is gone from every signature that offsets, including offsetCoord's -- that is why generics-sop no longer appears in contexts that have no other reason to mention it. The AffineSpace instance now asks for (All AffineSpace cs, All AdditiveGroup (MapDiff cs)). (3) A tuple literal is NOT a displacement: write ((-1) :| (-1) :| EmptyCoord), or coordFromTuple (-1,-1) / coordToTuple. Those two functions are arity-generic and are the only signatures left carrying IsProductType; keeping the conversion OUT of the class is deliberate, since an implicit coercion is what put the constraint in every consumer's context to begin with. The design follows manifolds' Needle: associated type, products get theirs structurally.

sized-grid: the missing Dolt remote is a deliberate choice, not an oversight. sized-grid session hygiene: sessions work on a .claude/worktrees branch. Check 'git branch --no-merged master' at session start BEFORE picking up an issue. Merge the SAME session you write the work -- historically nobody did, and four branches once held work whose issues were already CLOSED. As of 2026-08-11 master is at 53b86cd with no unmerged branches.

HOW TO MERGE FROM A WORKTREE SESSION: you cannot do it from inside the worktree. The harness refuses git commands aimed at the shared checkout (including ones the user types with the '!' prefix, which run in the same sandbox), and git will not let a worktree update a branch checked out elsewhere. Call ExitWorktree with action 'keep' first; the session returns to /Users/kevin/workspace/sized-grid and normal git works.

EnterWorktree branches from origin/master (worktree.baseRef defaults to 'fresh'), so if the beads auto-export commits to master DURING your session -- which it does -- your branch is behind and 'git merge --ff-only' fails. Use 'git merge --no-ff'. Do NOT rebase: the branch is already pushed, so rebasing would need a force-push, and rebasing your own merge commit replays it into the same .beads conflict.

DO NOT run 'git pull --rebase' before pushing master, despite CLAUDE.md saying to. It tries to flatten the merge commit and dies on the .beads/issues.jsonl conflict; 'git rebase --abort' recovers. Just check 'git status -sb' says ahead-N and push.

.beads/issues.jsonl CONFLICTS ON EVERY MERGE, because the auto-export hook writes it in the main checkout while you work. Resolve it by regenerating, never by hand: 'bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl' then 'git add'. Dolt is the source of truth and already holds both sides. Note the export orders memory lines non-deterministically, so a diff that touches only memory lines is noise, not a real change.

Each branch merges cleanly against master individually, so a clean 'git merge-tree' proves nothing; conflicts are between branches and the dangerous ones are semantic (a branch adding an export list while another adds top-level functions to the same file merges clean and leaves them unexported).

sized-grid beads export workflow (set up 2026-08-11): auto-export is now OFF. config.yaml carries export.auto=false and export.git-add=false, so bd no longer rewrites or git-adds .beads/issues.jsonl after every write. Two reasons it had to go: bd 1.0.3 defaults those to true (bd 1.1 flipped them to opt-in, calling the JSONL 'not the canonical source of truth, not cross-machine sync, not a full database backup'), and bd export orders the MEMORY lines non-deterministically -- back-to-back exports of an unchanged DB differ, which is what produced the endless phantom 4-add/4-delete diffs and the textual merge conflicts.

EXPORT MANUALLY, SORTED, once at session end -- always sorted, or the phantom churn returns:
  bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl && sort -o .beads/issues.jsonl .beads/issues.jsonl
Sorted output is byte-stable run to run and round-trips (bd import --dry-run reads back all issues + memories).

Merge conflicts on that path are handled by a merge driver: .gitattributes maps it to merge=beads, and LOCAL git config (not committed -- re-run in any fresh clone) defines:
  git config merge.beads.name 'regenerate beads JSONL from Dolt'
  git config merge.beads.driver 'bd export -o %A && sort -o %A %A'
This regenerates from the shared Dolt DB instead of merging text, which also fixes the old worktree problem: every worktree shares the MAIN checkout's .beads, so a worktree branch used to carry a stale issues.jsonl.

STILL TRUE: no Dolt remote is configured and .beads/backup/ is gitignored, so the git-tracked issues.jsonl remains the ONLY off-machine copy. Do not gitignore it. On bd >= 1.1 the export and driver both need --include-memories or the 7 memories silently vanish from the file.

TypeData (`type data`) has no application in sized-grid, checked 2026-08-12. The extension's whole value is for a data type you promote and never use at the term level; sized-grid has zero such types. Every data/newtype in src is a genuine runtime value (Extremum, Ordinal, Clamped, Periodic, Coord, OffGrid, Grid, FocusedGrid, GridSizeProof), and all type-level indexing comes from builtin kinds (Nat, [], Type) plus the coord types themselves -- which must stay inhabited because Coord cs = Coord (NP I cs) stores an I x per axis, and a type-data constructor has no inhabitants. Extremum is the tempting near-miss (closed AtMin/AtMax tag set) but it is the RESULT of axisBoundaryIsCoord :: c n -> Maybe Extremum, i.e. pure runtime -- exactly inverted. Also verified against GHC 9.12.3: GHC2024 does NOT imply TypeData (error GHC-15013), and type data fields must still have kind Type just like plain data ('type data P = MkP 5' is rejected identically), so type data buys namespace hygiene only, never new expressiveness.

GHC type-checker plugins are NOT transitive: enabling -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.Normalise / KnownNat.Solver in sized-grid only affects sized-grid's own modules. It cannot remove 'KnownNat (n * n)' from ../aoc signatures -- aoc solves its own constraints and does not enable the plugins (no 'typelits' in aoc.cabal/cabal.project/flake.nix). Any 'the plugin will simplify callers' reasoning about sized-grid's API is wrong; only an API change does that (see sized-grid-k6n: AllGridSizeKnown is a type FAMILY, so it emits KnownNat (MaxCoordSize ...) at the call site, whereas the AllSizedKnown CLASS solves the same obligation inductively with no plugin). Corollary: AllSizedKnown is load-bearing, not plumbing -- replacing it with a bare KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs) would push a plugin requirement onto downstream users. Also as of 2026-08-12 natnormalise 0.9.6 / knownnat 0.8.4 DROPPED ghc-tcplugins-extra for ghc-tcplugin-api 0.19 and build on GHC 9.14.1, lifting the old 9.14 blocker; nixpkgs still pins the 0.7.x line so flake.nix needs callHackageDirect overrides.

sized-grid: 'interior' (not onBoundary) and 'has a full 3^d-1 Moore neighbourhood' are the same set only on bounded (Clamped/Ordinal) axes. On a Periodic axis shorter than the neighbourhood diameter -- e.g. Coord '[Periodic 2, Periodic 2] -- every cell is interior yet has 3 neighbours, not 8, because axisSteps dedups offsets -1 and +1 onto the same cell. GHC will not unroll a fold over a type-level list written as a FUNCTION -- a where-helper closed over the dictionary, or generics-sop's cpara_SList with the step passed as an argument. Both are polymorphically recursive (the function calls itself at a shorter list), so GHC specialises the outermost call, stops, and leaves one shared worker taking the All c dictionary at run time. INLINABLE does not help, and neither does -fpolymorphic-specialisation -fspecialise-aggressively (measured: the worker comes out byte-for-byte identical). Only an INSTANCE METHOD gets the per-axis dictionary resolved at compile time, because then there is one statically-known instance per axis. This is why sized-grid's IsCoordList carries sizeAndPosition as a method rather than coordPosition having a where-helper: 320 B/call -> 0 B, and index over 90,000 coords went 27 MB -> 38 B. Applies to any generics-sop NP fold in this codebase.

sized-grid neighbourhoods: generate them PER AXIS, not by offsetting whole coordinates. Each axis enumerates the values reachable within r steps and keeps each value once at its true (minimal) step count; the cartesian product of per-axis-distinct sets is automatically distinct, and the centre is the only entry whose summed distance is 0. That buys deduplication with no nubOrd and no Ord (Coord cs), centre-exclusion with no Eq (Coord cs), and the correct WRAPPED distance on a torus. It also drops the constraint list from vonNeumanPoints' EIGHT (Enum/Num/Ord/All Integral (MapDiff cs)/AllDiffSame/All AffineSpace/Ord (CoordDiff cs)/IsProductType) to 'All IsCoordLifted cs' alone, and makes them work on Ordinal axes, which the AffineSpace-based versions never could -- Ordinal has no AffineSpace instance. Do not 'simplify' this back to mapping offsetCoord over a list of deltas: that reintroduces every one of those constraints and the duplicates.

sized-grid/generics-sop performance trap: getting 'sList' from an 'All c xs' dictionary is NOT free. SListI is All Top, so sList is computed by cpara_SList -- an allocating fold over the whole type-level list -- on every call. Core confirms it: 'case cpara_SList ($p2All $dAll) Proxy $WSNil sList1 of'. Any per-cell function that dispatches on 'case sList :: SList xs of' pays this per cell. Recursing structurally over an NP value instead (as coordPosition does) has no such cost. Same applies to the 'let irred = $p1All $dAll' thunks GHC emits to peel IsCoordLifted out of All at each level.

CORRECTION to memory ghc-will-not-unroll-a-fold-over-a: the claim that a fold fails to unroll because its step is a FUNCTION ARGUMENT is wrong. An eliminator with a higher-rank step (cpara_SList, or a clone) DOES unroll and constant-folds to a literal. The real variable is INLINE vs INLINABLE on the wrapper: INLINABLE makes GHC specialise, and specialisation lambda-lifts the higher-rank step into a shared worker holding the per-axis dictionary at run time; INLINE makes it inline at the call site and unroll. What remains true: (a) a SELF-RECURSIVE where-helper can never unroll, since GHC does not inline self-recursive bindings, verified with INLINE; (b) eliminator+INLINE only wins if the INLINE chain reaches a site where the type-level list is CONCRETE -- in sized-grid it does not, because coordPosition is called from polymorphic instance methods (index, gridIndex), and cpara_SList+INLINE measured WORSE than doing nothing (584 B/call, 50 MB on index x90000, vs 320 B / 27 MB baseline); (c) a class method is the robust shape because the instance chain resolves whenever the DICTIONARY is known, at specialisation, not only at inlining.

MaxCoordSize's (c n) type-application match is NOT fragile -- do not 'fix' it to go through CoordNat. Checked 2026-08-12 against GHC 9.12.3 with a standalone reproduction. The worry: 'type family MaxCoordSize ((c n) ': cs) = n * MaxCoordSize cs' (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:303) matches a type application, so it looks like it would get stuck when the axis head is a rigid type variable x rather than a concrete 'Clamped 5'. It does not. IsCoordLifted carries 'x ~ CoordContainer x (CoordNat x)' as a superclass (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:198), and that given equality refines x into application form, so the clause matches with c := CoordContainer x and n := CoordNat x. Verified: 'App (x ': xs) ~ (CoordNat x * App xs)' is provable from 'IsCoordLifted x' and NOT provable without it (negative control fails with GHC-18872), so the test has power. A CoordNat-based definition compiles equally, so it is a wash -- and the current poly-kinded '(cs :: [k])' signature is strictly more general than a CoordNat version, which would be pinned to '[Type]'. That superclass equality is exactly what IsCoordLifted exists to provide.

Type-checker plugins are not transitive, so they cannot fix a constraint that leaks into a consumer's signature. -fplugin applies only to the modules of the package that enables it; a downstream package solves its own wanteds with GHC alone. In sized-grid this means a leak like 'KnownNat (n*n)' escaping through an exported signature is only fixable by an API change (class instead of type family), never by adding ghc-typelits-knownnat here. Corollary for testing: any test of what a consumer must write has to be compiled WITHOUT the plugins -- sized-grid.cabal splits 'common lang-base' from 'common lang' and the 'downstream' test-suite imports the former for exactly this reason.
